ground:codebase.summary: Technical map of the current rule head (arc/model.py) and the old-repo design docs it comes from. Everything below was read from the files cited. The rule head is a per-lane lasso solved by block-coordinate ISTA, one proximal step per block, with step size 1. The variables are theta [L,13,p=64] and Gamma [L,F=K+1=9] (one scalar per frame, no colour index). It uses leave-one-out statistics over the other demonstration lanes of the group: G [L,p,p], S [L,13,p], plus C_k [L,F,13,p], H [L,F,F] and s [L,F] for the frames. These are normalised by the pooled count of labelled cells and recomputed every block from the current phi. The targets y are constant over recursion, and theta is the only thing that carries history. lambda is one global scalar (lam_floor + softplus(lam_raw)), shared by theta and Gamma, and it enters only through soft(). The carry {h, ek, ev, w, theta, gam, r} passes from block to block and from segment to segment. It is detached at segment boundaries, and theta/r/gam are also detached at the first gradient block. Proposition 4 holds structurally in the code: the only cross-lane operation is others@P in statistics(). Theorem 0 (conditions S/L/I/C), propositions 2 and 4, and the proposals to turn the bands accumulator W into the rule synapse (delta term plus proximal map) are located at exact lines in minimal_rule_synapse, cognitive_map section 8/12, theory_summary section 6 and rule_synapse_placement. The STDP negative results come from old docs/results.md lines 159-178 and the 10-17 doc. Two findings bear directly on design. (1) In this repo's <=10 E1 runs, lambda=0 and lambda=0.01 give the same exact counts in all four settings. lambda does make theta sparse, but sparsity is not load-bearing for the current content map. In the old standalone toy the threshold was decisive for an explicit position operator (95% vs 25/400). (2) At lambda=0, the update theta <- theta(I-G)+S is exactly a batched delta rule (DeltaNet/Widrow-Hoff form). It is a fast-weight accumulator whose decay is the data-dependent matrix (I-G), compared with the scalar/complex decay of the bands. This gives a clean single-family account of both memories. Condition C (convergence) is not met by the current single-step iteration.

findings.claim: State shapes and initial values (initial_carry): h [L,T=2C^2=1800,d=512] = init_hidden; ek, ev [L,H=8,T,2*dh*R] (dh=64, R=4 bands) zeros; bands w [L,H,dh,dh] zeros; theta [L,13,p] zeros with p=cfg.phi=64; gam [L,K+1] zeros (only when frames>0; K=8 in configs/arc1.json and arc2.json); r [L,O=C^2=900,13] zeros. theta is per LANE, not per group.

findings.claim: Features: phi(o) = W_phi h(o) / (||W_phi h(o)|| + 1e-6), only on the O output-canvas cells (h[:, O:]). W_phi = Linear(d -> p=64, bias=False). So phi is unit-length up to the eps and ||phi||^2 <= 1.

findings.relevance: Unit phi is what makes tr G <= 1, which licenses step size 1.

findings.claim: Leave-one-out statistics: w = m*demo, where m = (label != PAD) covers colour cells AND EOS cells of the output canvas, and demo is a per-lane flag. Per-lane raw sums: P_G = sum_o w phi phi^T [p,p]; P_S = sum_o w onehot13(y) phi^T [13,p]. With frames: C_k = sum_o w kappa_k phi^T [F,13,p]; H_kj = sum_o w <kappa_k,kappa_j> [F,F]; s_k = sum_o w <kappa_k,y> [F]. others[l,l'] = (group_l == group_l') AND l != l' (0/1 [L,L]). n_l = max(1, sum_{l' in others} sum_o w_{l'}) is the POOLED count of labelled cells over the other demo lanes. Each statistic = (others @ P)/n_l. Weighting is per cell, so demos with larger grids weigh more. y, m and demo are computed once per segment from batch labels and are constant over every block.

findings.claim: Implied objective (derived by matching terms, checked against the code): J_l(theta,Gamma) = (1/2n_l) sum_{l' != l, same group, demo} sum_{o labelled} ||onehot y(o) - theta phi(o) - sum_k Gamma_k kappa_k(o)||^2 + lambda(||theta||_1 + ||Gamma||_1). In step(), g = theta G - S + sum_k Gamma_k C_k is dJ/dtheta, and gg_k = <theta,C_k>_F + (H Gamma)_k - s_k is dJ/dGamma_k. No bias term, no prior centre: theta_0 = 0 and the threshold pulls toward 0.

findings.claim: Iteration: block Gauss-Seidel with ONE proximal step per block per variable, step size 1. First theta <- soft(theta - g, lambda), then Gamma <- soft(Gamma - gg(theta_new), lambda). Validity as written in the docstrings: lambda_max(G) <= tr G <= 1; for Gamma, sum_k ||kappa_k||^2 <= 1 because every kappa is divided by sqrt(K+1), so lambda_max(H) <= 1. Step 1 = 1/trace bound is conservative compared with 1/lambda_max(G).

findings.claim: lambda: one global scalar, lambda = lam_floor + softplus(lam_raw). It is shared by theta and Gamma, has the same value at every block, segment and lane, and has no per-colour or per-iteration schedule. It enters ONLY in step() as the soft-threshold level. Init lam_init = 1e-3. With lam_learn=False, lam_raw is a buffer equal to -inf, so lambda = lam_floor exactly. Weight decay on lam_raw only when decay_lam (train.py). The ARC-2 run used a fixed 0.005. Theoretical prior: kappa/sqrt(n) with kappa = 0.145 (universal threshold 3.67*sqrt(p_c/(64n))). Learned lambda at <=10 is about 0.5x the theory value (0.0057 vs 0.011).

findings.claim: Read and frames: r(o) = theta phi(o) + sum_k Gamma_k kappa_k(o) [L,O,13], computed in FP32 with autocast off. kappa_0 = colour histogram of the lane's own input grid (tokens 2..11). kappa_k for k=1..K is a softmax read from output cell o over the live input cells t of the SAME lane: score <rope_k(W_fq h(o)), rope_k(W_fk h(t))>/sqrt(E), value onehot(x_in(t)). frame_omega [K,2,E/4] holds learned row/col frequencies (init periods logspace 2..4C; frame_fixed makes it a buffer). All kappa are divided by sqrt(K+1). Gamma has no colour index, so frames copy input colours by learned position and any colour remapping is only in theta.

findings.claim: Feedback and logits: fb = W_fb r, where W_fb = Linear(13 -> d, no bias) initialised to ZERO. fb is added to the embedding on output-canvas tokens, and the block input is u = h + sqrt(d)*[emb_in ; emb_out + fb]. The r used at block i is the previous head's read. Default (out_ffn False, direct_head True): logits = classifier(h_out-canvas) + tau*r, with tau a learned scalar initialised to 1 (a buffer if tau_learn False). out_ffn: logits = classifier(RMSNorm(v + SwiGLU(v))), v = RMSNorm(h + sqrt(d) W_fb r), with no tau*r term. direct_head False (r-only): logits = classifier.bias + tau*r.
findings.relevance: The demos->query channel is r (13-dim per cell) through W_fb and through tau*r. This is the narrow channel the S-violation diagnosis points at.

findings.claim: Carry and detach: the carry {h, ek, ev, w, theta, gam, r} is passed from block to block and from segment to segment. segment() returns every entry detached. Blocks 0..blocks-grad_blocks-1 run under no_grad. At i == blocks - grad_blocks, theta, r and gam are explicitly detached ('the no-grad blocks' head state enters as a constant'). Gradients flow through the last grad_blocks ISTA steps (the soft threshold's a.e. derivative, into lam_raw, phi/W_phi, kappa/W_fq/W_fk/frame_omega, and r -> W_fb -> the next block), but not across segments. Group lifetime is loops=16 segments x 8 blocks = 128 ISTA steps for theta. In the <=10 harness loops=1, so theta restarts from 0 each step.

findings.claim: Rule-head statistics have NO temporal memory. G and S are recomputed each block from the current phi only, with no trace or EMA over recursion, and y is constant. theta, through the warm start, is the only history. With y constant, any asymmetric temporal kernel applied to S would only filter phi and could not express order (the handoff states this).

findings.claim: Proposition 4 holds structurally in the code. bands_step/BandsRead sum over tokens T inside each lane (batch dim B = lanes). Frames attend from output cells to input cells of the same lane. The ONLY cross-lane operation in the model is others @ P in statistics().
findings.relevance: Any replacement must keep the cross-lane coupling confined to the rule-synapse statistics, or proposition 4 is lost.

findings.claim: Leakage (condition N). At evaluation, test lanes have demo=False, so their labels never enter any statistics; N holds structurally. Demo lanes are scored with the theta of the other demos and used as the tie-break. In training every lane is demo=True and query=True, so leave-one-out excludes a lane's labels only at first order. There is a second-order path one block later: y_A -> S_B -> theta_B -> r_B -> W_fb -> h_B -> phi_B -> (G_A, S_A) -> theta_A. Whether the model exploits it has not been measured.

findings.claim: Bands memory as implemented, per head and per token position over block time. E_K,r <- z_r E_K,r + gamma_r k~; D_V,r = z_r E_V,r; E_V,r <- D_V,r + gamma_r v; k_mix = sum_r Re(a_r E_K,r); v_mix = sum_r Re(b_r D_V,r); S = v^T k_mix + v_mix^T k~ ([D,D], summed over tokens); W <- (1-eta)W + eta S; read = q~ (v^T k~ + W)^T. Pairs are the same token at different blocks. Kernel: K+(lag>=0) = sum_r gamma_r Re(a_r z_r^lag), which includes lag 0 inside S; K-(lag>=1) = sum_r gamma_r Re(b_r z_r^lag). On top of this, the same-block Hebbian sum v k~^T with fixed gain 1 is read directly and is not in W. eta = sigmoid(eta_raw) is capped at outer_eta = 0.125. z_r = exp(-e^nu + i theta), gamma_r = sqrt(1-|z_r|^2). Name clash: the bands S [D x D] is a different object from the rule-head S [13 x p].

findings.claim: Theorem 0 (old repo). Given Pi and B fixed, if S (f_tau in H_0), L (Delta_tau = W_tau - W0_tau is s-sparse in G-coordinates), I (the demo measurement A_D has the null-space property of order s in G-coordinates) and C (the iteration converges, lambda -> 0+) all hold, then the M0 prediction on the query is exact. Proof: as lambda -> 0+ the lasso minimiser becomes the min-l1 Delta with A_D Delta = b; NSP makes it unique. Necessity remarks: S fails -> no selection rule can work; I fails -> another Delta' with equal or smaller l1 may answer differently. The full conditions table also has F (format), W (l1 selection), M (prior centre = puzzle embedding), N (no leakage), G (gradient through the unrolled iteration). The NSP statement is in section 4.4.

findings.claim: Proposition 4 (old repo): slow heads see only within a grid; the rule head sees only between pairs; no other cross-grid path. Reason: if slow attention linked demo and query grids, slow weights would do in-context learning, the selection principle would no longer be 'l1 + prior centre', and theorem 0 would guarantee nothing. Routing everything through the fast weight (a lasso solution) fixes the selection principle by structure. Restated in cognitive_map section 12.1 as one of only four structural items.

findings.claim: Old proposals to make the bands accumulator W the rule synapse, with a delta term and a proximal map. (a) 10-20 placement: W <- soft(W + eta (value - W key) (x) (trace-filtered key trace), theta); the error removes source ambiguity A-bar and the threshold selects support; FISTA needs 100-150 iterations versus 16 blocks. (b) minimal section 6: the delta term expands to cross pairs (output cell <-> same demo's input cells) minus W times the autocorrelation within the input grid. Promotion needs (a) key = position code (learned RoPE as G), (b) pairs chosen by slot membership, not time lag (packing breaks lag), (c) accumulator + proximal map. (c) minimal section 9.2: write = cross-attention map minus W-hat times self-attention map; lineage linear attention = fast weights (Schlag 2021) -> DeltaNet; the rule head stores a QK map. (d) minimal section 9.4: the bands accumulator W becomes W-hat; traces and windows stay as slow perception. (e) cognitive_map section 8: code g = learned RoPE; memory M_b = Hebbian sum of RoPE keys with the time window replaced by 'same grid, same frame'; rule synapse = accumulator + delta + prox (group-sparse + l1, prior centre); the procedure is still open in section 12.6. (f) theory_summary section 6: one local plasticity rule does pairing (Hebbian sum y k^T), decorrelation (-W sum k k^T, Yule-Walker) and selection (soft threshold). Because traces are linear, they hold sufficient statistics, so the prox step can be iterated many times on small matrices and condition C becomes real. Band decay forgets stale statistics, and multiple bands give multiple time scales. Constraints: windows must follow slot membership or RoPE relative position; perception stays softmax. (g) 10-22 handoff: same hybrid hypothesis.

findings.claim: Old placement section 2: bands time windows are LINEAR in the data. They cannot zero individual synapse entries; forgetting |z|^2 is L2-like proportional decay; signed-window cancellation is data-independent. Section 3.1: with discrete colour keys, least squares alone is exact for the colour map (no threshold needed). Section 3.2: the delta-rule fixed point dW = V Phi^T (Phi Phi^T + lambda I)^-1 is zero outside the span of the demo phis, so l1 in a structure-code basis is needed for POSITION operators. Section 0: in the standalone toy rule_syn, a threshold recovered rules from 3 demos at 95%; without a threshold 25/400; with a flattened 64x64 joint matrix 0-2/400.

findings.claim: 10-17 time-dependent plasticity doc. Window even/odd decomposition: the even part is Hebb-type, the odd part stores order; online computation needs BOTH pre and post traces. Hebb term = 0th moment (net area) of the window; 1st moment = TD-like order term. For an antisymmetric window integrated over one block, L(0)=0, so a gain-1 same-block Hebb is a separately chosen c0*delta(s). EMA bounds |W| <= max|dW|/eta. With odd-only windows the read vanishes at fixed points: exp-STDP without EMA swung 67.1 -> 55.6 -> 68.0% held-out, and the 10k extrapolation peaked at 3 segments. KV-EMA (delayed Hebb) had fewer early solves (181 vs 330 at 7.8k). It criticises exp_hebb: Hebb not derived from the window, and the even part read directly while the odd part goes through the EMA. Proposed cleanest candidate (section 3.5): a block-integrated continuous window with free area so L(0) > 0; one window gives both Hebb and order; risk that learning drives the area to 0 or below.

Accumulated phase offset: omega does not go to 0. Integrate/leaky generators: alpha switches off / batch memorisation. Angle-displacement clock: no time passes between blocks, take-off at 33k. Leaky model B took off 4-6k later; B-EMA had no delay (1,090 vs 1,087, extrapolation 11.1%). bands 16 blocks/segment, 10k-block extrapolation: 306 -> 420, error reduction 55.3%, no relapse, 89/92 unsolved puzzles wander.

findings.claim: Algebraic identity (derived, exact). At lambda=0 one step is theta_{t+1} = theta_t (I - G_t) + S_t, with G = (1/n) sum phi phi^T and S = (1/n) sum y phi^T over the other demos' labelled cells. This is the DeltaNet / Widrow-Hoff form W <- W(I - beta k k^T) + beta v k^T, batched over demo cells with beta = 1/n. It is a fast-weight accumulator whose forgetting is the data-dependent matrix (I - G_t) instead of the bands' scalar (1 - eta) or complex z_r. For fixed phi and theta_0 = 0, theta_T = S G^+ (I - (I - G)^T) on range(G): truncated Landweber, which converges to the minimum-Frobenius-norm least-squares solution as T grows. With lambda > 0 the step is ISTA (LCA in neural terms). Literature names (DeltaNet, Landweber, early stopping as regularisation, LCA/Rozell 2008) are cited from memory and need checking.

findings.relevance: Gives one clean family for both memories (Hebbian accumulation + decay operator). The rule head's lineage (Hebb -> fast weight -> delta/DeltaNet) can be stated without new terms.

design_implications: One family for both memories: both are fast-weight accumulators over recursion depth. Bands (within a lane, per head): W <- (1-eta)W + eta * sum_lag K(lag) post(x)pre, plus the gain-1 tonic term. Rule synapse (across lanes, within a group): theta <- theta(I - G) + S [+ prox]. They differ only in the decay operator (scalar/complex z_r vs data-dependent I - G) and in pairing (same token at different depths vs same cell index across demo lanes). Stating the architecture this way, Hebbian S + anti-Hebbian decorrelation G + optional proximal map, needs no new terms and keeps proposition 4 intact.

The lasso is not empirically load-bearing for the current content map theta: E1 shows lambda=0 equal to lambda=0.01, and ISTA-30 gives at most about +4. The old theory agrees: l1 was argued, and shown on a toy (95% vs 25/400), only for explicit POSITION operators. For discrete colour keys, least squares is exact (placement section 3.1). The cleanest story is either (a) drop lambda and restate theorem 0 with the implicit bias of the delta rule from theta_0=0 (min-norm least squares; Landweber for finite T), with I' = query phi lies in the span of the demo phis and C' = convergence or early-stopping regularisation; or (b) keep l1 only for a future position/transition operator, where it is theoretically needed. Claiming 'l1 is the selection principle' for the current head contradicts the repo's own data.

Condition C does not describe the deployed head (one step per block, step 1 = 1/trG rather than 1/lambda_max, phi moving every block, 8-128 total steps). If the paper keeps theorem 0, it must say it holds for the lasso solution at a coupled fixed point (section 10.3a), not for the implemented iterate. Alternatively, adopt the old section 6 proposal: decaying trace-like sufficient statistics plus many cheap prox iterations on 64x64 matrices per block. That is the one concrete path that makes C true, at negligible token cost.

A temporal (STDP-like) kernel inside the rule synapse is meaningless as long as y is constant across recursion: it would only low-pass phi. For STDP and the rule synapse to meet in one head, the head must regress something that changes along recursion. One option is a transition head phi(t) -> phi(t+1) solved from demo trajectories and applied to the query (handoff section 3.6). This is also the most direct way to widen hypothesis family S toward procedural ARC-2 rules without hand-coded operators. The torus toy's learned generator composition (100% on unseen transforms) is the supporting evidence.

Every block's theta regresses the same final colours (no intermediate targets). Multi-step composition currently has to be carried by perception re-processing the 13-dim r through W_fb. This is the precise locus of the ARC-2 S-violation, and a better-designed head should give the recursion its own per-step target or state.

For precision in the writeup: proposition 4 holds exactly in code (the only cross-lane op is others@P). Condition N holds exactly at evaluation (test demo=0) but only at first order in training: own labels can return one block later via other lanes' feedback-shaped phi. Condition M (prior centre) is intentionally absent (it hurt Mini-ARC). The deployed family is r = theta phi + Gamma.kappa with Gamma scalar per frame (no colour index), not the cognitive-map A_j/Pi_j/omega_j family.

Bands elegance gap carried over from the 10-17 critique: the gain-1 same-block Hebbian is read directly, outside the learned kernel, while the kernel goes through the EMA. The 10-17 section 3.5 candidate (block-integrated window with free area, so L(0) > 0) would let one learned kernel produce both the Hebbian DC term and the odd order term, matching the paper's 'STDP generalises Hebb' thesis. The documented risk is that the area learns to 0 (seen in exp-STDP; Sudoku heads drove the net fixed-point gain to about 0 in 7 of 8). The tonic term is the safety net the handoff calls an implementation detail.

Notation hazards for the paper: the bands S [D x D] and the rule-head S [13 x p] collide, and so do G (the old structure-code matrix) and G (the Gram matrix). Rename in the text, for example C_yphi for the cross-covariance and Sigma_phi for the Gram. Do not reuse the internal names 'TDP' or 'sparse LTD'.

ground:theory.summary:
Short answer to the user's question (would the architecture and its explanation come out elegant, not just swapped in?): the explanation does, a lot. A real swap of the mechanism does not.

(1) The current rule head already is a competition network. The unit-step ISTA step in arc/model.py step() is exactly one forward-Euler step (dt/tau = 1) of the LCA (Rozell 2008):
- S = Hebbian drive (teacher x pre).
- theta G = anti-Hebbian term (own read x pre). It acts as lateral inhibition among the synapses onto one colour unit, with strength G_jk = how often their presynaptic features fire together over the demo cells.
- soft threshold = constant-size depression with a floor at 0. With signed synapses split into two rectified populations (Dale), it is a uniform depression of both.
'Replacing the lasso with LCA' is a renaming. The code and theorem 0 stay exactly as they are.

(2) One proposition reconciles the STDP thesis with theorem 0. Give the Hebbian and anti-Hebbian terms any two-sided kernel over recursion with positive DC gain that is the same for every colour. Then the converged rule is a positive multiple of a lasso solution: theta = (k_h/k_a) lasso(lambda/k_h). At lambda -> 0+ the query argmax is the same. The odd lobe vanishes on any constant trajectory, so it only shapes the path (at best it acts as a learned momentum, like FISTA or LISTA with weight coupling). In one line: the guarantee lives in the DC (Hebbian) part, the trajectory in the odd part.

(3) TEM's own memory update links the two theses. Whittington 2020 (checked in the paper text): M <- lambda M + eta (p - p_hat)(p + p_hat)^T. Over the sequence prediction -> observation, this is a two-time kernel with classical STDP signs and zero total DC, and it vanishes when the prediction is correct. The rule synapse's delta (y - r_hat) phi^T is its hetero-associative (colour from features) version.

What is not elegant:
- Making timing change the converged answer requires leaving convexity. Hard threshold / k-WTA (IHT) or an EM-style fit-based soft-WTA mixture would do it. With noiseless demos, every exact fit whose nonzero entries exceed the threshold is a hard-threshold fixed point. Six starts gave six different dense fits, none the 3-sparse truth. Selection then lives in the start state and the path, and a guarantee needs RIP of order 3s instead of the null-space property. In our check, k-WTA also recovered the rule less often than the lasso.
- A constant teacher y leaves the odd lobe inert: it collapses to a filter of the pre features.
- The odd lobe does real work only with a predict-then-observe event: it then yields exactly the delta rule, provided the post-leading lobe is LTD-like. But a full clamp/release cycle cancels exactly, so the plasticity window or a third factor has to stop at the event.
- None of these variants touches the ARC-2 failure, which is the hypothesis family (condition S).

Recommendation: rewrite the explanation (LCA/delta reading, the fixed-point proposition, the TEM bridge), keep the code, and do not claim that STDP improves rule selection on the rule synapse.

All propositions were checked numerically in float64 (scripts in the scratchpad). Literature claims are marked web-checked or from memory.

findings.claim: (a) The current rule-head update theta <- soft(theta - (theta G - S), lam) is exactly one forward-Euler step with dt/tau = 1 of the LCA (Locally Competitive Algorithm): u_{t+1} = u_t + (S - u_t - theta_t (G - I)), theta = soft(u, lam). The membrane state u is implicit: u_{t+1} = theta_t + (S - theta_t G). So the lasso head already is an LCA competition network, and 'replacing it with LCA' changes no code.
findings.source: Algebra on arc/model.py step(); numerical check (max difference 2.8e-14 over 500 steps), scratchpad/theory/checks.py #1; Rozell, Johnson, Baraniuk & Olshausen 2008, Neural Computation 20(10) (from memory, verify)
findings.relevance: The paper can present the rule head as a plasticity/competition circuit without changing code or theorem 0. This is the 'elegant explanation' half of the user's question.

findings.claim: (a) Leaky LCA u <- (1-alpha) u + alpha (S - theta (G - I)) has, for every alpha in (0,1], fixed points exactly at the lasso optimality (KKT) conditions, and it converges. Proof: soft is firmly nonexpansive, and I - G has spectrum in [0,1] because lambda_max(G) <= tr G = 1, so T(u) = soft(u)(I - G) + S is averaged and the iteration is a Krasnosel'skii-Mann iteration. Also, u is a one-sided exponential trace over recursion of the delta drive, with DC gain 1.
findings.source: Derivation; numerical check: alpha = 0.2/0.5/1 all reach the FISTA lasso solution within 2e-13 with KKT residual < 1e-14 (checks.py #2); Balavoine, Romberg & Rozell 2012, IEEE TNNLS 23(9):1377-1389 (web-checked: LCA converges to the optimum when it is unique) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3816963
findings.relevance: The simplest temporally asymmetric rule synapse (a causal eligibility trace on the drive) already keeps theorem 0. A learned two-sided kernel generalises the LCA time constant.

findings.claim: (a) Term-by-term reading. theta G - S = (1/n) sum_o (theta phi(o) - y(o)) phi(o)^T. S is teacher x pre (Hebbian). theta G is own-read x pre (anti-Hebbian). In LCA coordinates, the synapses theta_{c,j} onto colour unit c inhibit each other with strength G_jk, the co-activity of presynaptic features j and k over the demo cells. G (pre x pre) and S (teacher x pre) are themselves same-time Hebbian outer-product fast memories, the same kind of object as the bands W. The soft threshold is a constant-size depression toward 0 with a floor.
findings.source: Identity from arc/model.py statistics() and step()
findings.relevance: Gives the precise version of 'theta G is anti-Hebbian lateral inhibition, S is Hebbian drive' with no new terms. The bands and the rule head become one kind of object (outer-product fast memories).

findings.claim: (e) Signed synapses as a Dale split: theta = theta_plus - theta_minus with theta_plus, theta_minus >= 0, each updated by the same delta term, a uniform activity-independent depression lam, and rectification at 0. This has the same fixed point as the lasso, and at the optimum the two populations never overlap (theta_plus * theta_minus = 0). So the 'LTD-like' part of the soft threshold is a uniform depression of two rectified populations, and a signed synapse is a differential pair.
findings.source: Standard lasso <-> nonnegative-split equivalence; numerical check: max difference 9.8e-15, overlap count 0 (checks.py #10)
findings.relevance: Gives the requested signed-activity definition: LTP-/LTD-like is defined on the association (toward or away from v k^T, or toward or away from 0 for |theta|), not on the sign of individual entries.

findings.claim: (a, hard threshold) Hard threshold / IHT with a fixed threshold mu, noiseless demos: every exact fit (theta G = S) whose nonzero entries all exceed mu is a fixed point, because the gradient is zero on and off the support. The fixed point therefore carries no sparsity selection, and selection moves entirely into the start state and the path. The soft threshold keeps a unique selection (minimum L1).
findings.source: One-line proof; numerical check, n=16 cells, p=40, true s=3: six starts gave six different exact-fit fixed points (residual < 1e-12) with 35-40 nonzeros each, none the truth; the soft threshold gave the same point from every start (spread 1.8e-15) (checks.py #4)
findings.relevance: Core trade-off: temporal asymmetry can matter for the answer only where the fixed point does not settle the selection, i.e. in the nonconvex (L0) regime, and there the theorem-0 guarantee is lost.

findings.claim: (a, k-WTA) Keeping the s largest |u| (k-WTA) is IHT's top-s projection. The theorem-0 analogue for it needs (I') RIP of order 3s in the learned code; delta_3s < 1/sqrt(32) is the constant attributed to Blumensath & Davies 2009, plus (C') convergence from theta = 0. RIP_3s is stronger than the null-space property the lasso needs. Numerically, with p=64, s=4 and step 1/lambda_max, IHT recovered the rule less often than the lasso at lam -> 0: 0.10 vs 0.725 at n=20 and 0.50 vs 1.00 at n=30 (40 trials each).
findings.source: checks.py #5; Blumensath & Davies 2009, Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis 27(3):265-274 (citation web-checked; the delta_3s < 1/sqrt(32) constant confirmed only through a secondary source, arXiv:1005.4539, which should be checked against the original) https://arxiv.org/pdf/1005.4539
findings.relevance: A hard competitive rule synapse can keep an exactness guarantee only under a stronger identification condition, and in practice it needs more demonstrations.

findings.claim: (c) Fixed-point invariance. Filter the Hebbian term (teacher x pre) and the anti-Hebbian term (read x pre) with two-sided kernels over recursion (pre-leading K+, post-leading K-, same-time K0) of DC gains k_h, k_a > 0, any shape and any odd part. If perception converges to a constant phi*, the limit is theta = (k_h/k_a) lasso(G*, S*, lam/k_h). The odd part contributes exactly zero on a constant trajectory. A positive scalar does not change the argmax, so theorem 0 (lam -> 0+) holds for every such kernel. Only the transient differs.
findings.source: Derivation; numerical check with odd kernels of DC 1.0 and 0.8 and geometrically converging phi: limit equals the predicted scaled lasso within 2.3e-13; query argmax agreement with the plain lasso 1.0; distance after 30 steps 2.43 (same-time kernel) vs 3.17 (two-sided) (checks.py #3, #3b)
findings.relevance: The central proposition reconciling the main thesis (STDP generalises Hebb: its DC part is the Hebbian term) with theorem 0: the guarantee lives in the DC part, the trajectory in the odd part. One formalism covers the bands and the rule synapse.

findings.claim: (c) Two conditions on the kernel. (i) Post-side (colour) DC gains must be the same for every colour: colour-dependent gains rescale the rows of theta and change the argmax. Colour-permutation equivariance forces colour-uniform post kernels, so this holds by symmetry. (ii) Per-feature pre-side DC gains d_j on both terms give a weighted lasso with lam_j = lam/d_j, which changes the L1 metric (the selection prior). The 'delay-weighted lasso' idea is exactly this, and it is a DC effect, not an odd-lobe effect. With non-leaky accumulation stopped at a finite T, d_j(T) is about 1 - latency_j/T: features that settle early are cheaper, and the effect vanishes as T grows (derivation; its practical relevance is a conjecture).
findings.source: Derivation; numerical check: weighted-lasso fixed point matches within 2.1e-13; query argmax agreement 0.998 with the same gain for every colour (finite lam 1e-4) vs 0.878 with colour-dependent gains (checks.py #7, #8)
findings.relevance: Says exactly where a temporal kernel could change the selection principle at convergence (pre-side per-feature DC only), and that colour symmetry protects the argmax.

findings.claim: (c) Where asymmetry changes the solution. (i) Perception that does not converge: on a cycling orbit, the averaged fixed point solves a monotone variational inequality theta G_K - k S_bar in lam d|theta|. Here G_K = sum_tau K(tau) C(tau), where C(tau) is the lag-tau correlation of phi along the orbit. Its skew part sum_tau K_odd(tau)(C(tau) - C(tau)^T) measures the orbit's circulation, and the solution then minimises no objective. (ii) Stopping at a finite number of blocks. (iii) A nonconvex rule synapse (hard / k-WTA / mixture), where the transient picks the basin. (iv) The joint (perception, theta) system is nonconvex anyway: theorem 0 is conditional on the phi* actually reached, and a rule-synapse kernel can change which joint fixed point that is.
findings.source: Derivation; numerical check on a period-12 cycling orbit with slow theta: skew part 0.027 for the odd kernel vs 3e-18 for its even part; the limit matches the averaged variational-inequality solution within 2e-4 (order of the step size); odd and even kernels with the same DC give limits differing by 0.034 (about 3% of the norm) (checks.py #11)
findings.relevance: Gives the honest scope of the main thesis: STDP over recursion changes the rule synapse's answer only for wandering perception (as in the 89/92 unsolved Sudoku puzzles), finite T, or a nonconvex selection.

findings.claim: (c) In the convex regime, a temporal term that is neutral at the fixed point can at most act as a learned momentum. FISTA's momentum is such a term and speeds convergence from O(1/k) to O(1/k^2) (Beck & Teboulle 2009, from memory). For learned unrolled ISTA, Chen, Liu, Wang & Yin 2018 identify a weight structure ('partial weight coupling') that the learned weights must satisfy for the network to converge to the true sparse signal; with it they prove linear convergence. This is the same principle: learned dynamics may differ only in the transient. Side note: the current step 1 <= 1/lambda_max(G) is valid but can be far below the best step 1/lambda_max when the features are spread (tr G = 1, p = 64). So finite-block convergence is where a kernel or momentum could actually help.
findings.source: Chen, Liu, Wang & Yin, NeurIPS 2018, arXiv:1808.10038 (web-checked) https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.10038 ; Beck & Teboulle 2009, SIAM J. Imaging Sciences (from memory, verify)
findings.relevance: A citable precedent for 'transient differs, fixed point preserved', and a precise statement of the most a rule-synapse kernel can buy.

findings.claim: (d) The y-constant problem, precisely: with post = y for all t, sum_{tau>0} K+(tau) y phi_{t-tau}^T + (K0 + sum K-) y phi_t^T. The post-leading lobe collapses to a same-time gain, and the two-sided kernel reduces to a one-sided causal filter of phi, so it cannot represent order.
findings.source: Algebra
findings.relevance: Confirms the handoff's worry and pins it down: with a constant teacher, the order information is gone.

findings.claim: (d) Teacher as an event. With pre phi constant and post jumping from the read r_hat to y at block t0, the transition adds exactly -M1^- (y - r_hat) phi^T (with M1^- = sum_tau tau K-(tau)) on top of the steady term K_bar post phi^T. This is the delta rule with a positive rate if and only if the post-leading lobe is LTD-like, i.e. the classical STDP sign. But a full clamp-then-release cycle with constant pre cancels exactly, so only the DC part survives. The plasticity window must therefore stop at the predict -> observe event (or be gated by a third factor).
findings.source: Derivation; numerical check: transition term matches within 2.2e-16, clamp/release cycle residual 2.1e-15 (checks.py #6); consistent with Xie & Seung, NIPS 1999 (web-checked abstract: antisymmetric timing rule ~ rule on the time derivative of the post rate) https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/1999/hash/c0560792e4a3c79e62f76cbf9fb277dd-Abstract.html and Bengio, Mesnard, Fischer, Zhang & Wu 2017, Neural Computation 29(3):555-577 (web-checked abstract: pre rate x rate of change of post approximates backprop) https://dblp.org/rec/journals/neco/BengioMFZW17
findings.relevance: The timing that makes the odd lobe meaningful is predict-then-observe within each step, a window that stops at the event, and an LTD-like post-leading lobe. Without the window limit or a gate it cancels.

findings.claim: TEM's memory update is M_t = lambda M_{t-1} + eta (p_t - p_hat_t)(p_t + p_hat_t)^T. Here p_hat is generated from the inferred grid code (the prediction) and p is inferred with the sensory input; TEM forms p as an elementwise product of the grid and sensory inputs, equivalent to an outer product. Expanding over the two-point sequence (p_hat, then p): +p p^T - p_hat p_hat^T (same-time lobes, + later, - earlier) and +p p_hat^T - p_hat p^T (pre-leading +1 LTP-like, post-leading -1 LTD-like). This is a two-time kernel with classical STDP signs and total DC zero, and it vanishes when the prediction equals the observation. The rule synapse's (y - r_hat) phi^T = S - theta G is its hetero-associative version.
findings.source: Whittington et al. 2020, Cell 183(5):1249-1263, STAR Methods (update equation and the elementwise-product / outer-product construction web-checked in the PMC text) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7707106 ; expansion is algebra
findings.relevance: The most elegant single formula for the paper: it joins thesis 1 (asymmetric kernel over time) and thesis 2 (TEM structure/content memory), and identifies the current S - theta G as TEM-type prediction-error Hebbian learning.

findings.claim: (d) A three-factor rule with a temporal-difference modulator (d_theta proportional to M_t e_t, with M_t = change in demo consistency, which needs no query answer) vanishes on any stationary trajectory, so like the odd lobe it does not move the fixed point. In the convex rule synapse it only changes the path. In a nonconvex or discrete search it changes the basin, matching the torus toy (revisits 0.35 -> 0.09, success@64 0.72 -> 0.96). The modulator supplies the event timing the constant teacher lacks, and the eligibility kernel sets how far back credit reaches. Conjecture: the useful trace length matches the feedback-loop latency (r -> W_fb -> perception -> phi takes at least 1 block). With exploration noise, E[M xi] is approximately -sigma^2 grad F (weight perturbation; Fiete & Seung 2006, from memory).
findings.source: Derivation (the stationary-point neutrality is immediate); torus results from /workspace/arc1-coupled/docs/handoff_toy_torus_search_2026-10-28.md; Fiete & Seung 2006 PRL; Fremaux & Gerstner 2016 (from memory, verify)
findings.relevance: Gives a single principle: signals that vanish at stationarity (odd lobes, TD modulators) are guarantee-neutral, and they matter for selection only in nonconvex landscapes. It also explains why the trace added little in the torus toy (one-step credit is enough there).

findings.claim: (b) Mixture of sparse experts whose gates g(o) = softmax(W_g h(o)) come from the lane's own perception (slow weights): r(o) = sum_m g_m(o) theta_m phi(o) = Theta [g(o) (x) phi(o)]. This is exactly one lasso on the product code psi = g (x) phi; |psi| <= 1, so step 1 stays valid. It is convex, theorem 0 holds as stated with psi, and a group lasso over experts (convex) picks few experts. psi is a TEM-like conjunctive code. Its hypothesis family is still 'linear in a learned per-cell feature', so it adds structure (case splits) but no expressivity beyond a wider phi.
findings.source: Identity; numerical check: maximum difference 4.4e-16 (checks.py #9)
findings.relevance: If rule units are added, gating by perception is the elegant version that keeps the guarantee. It does not fix ARC-2's family (S) failure.

findings.claim: (b) Gating by fit (soft-WTA responsibilities computed from the demo fit at temperature 1/beta) is block-coordinate descent on J(pi, theta) = sum_o sum_m pi_m(o) 0.5 |y - theta_m phi|^2 + lam sum_m |theta_m|_1 - (1/beta) H(pi). Each block is an exact softmax step or a weighted-lasso (LCA) step, so J decreases monotonically. The fixed points are only stationary points. The hard limit (beta -> inf) is a K-subspace-type clustering, NP-hard in general. Theorem 0 holds per expert only if the assignment is correct. The query also needs a separate gate (y is missing there), which is a second fast synapse. Local recovery results for mixed linear regression exist (Yi, Caramanis & Sanghavi 2014; Balakrishnan, Wainwright & Yu 2017; L1 version: Stadler, Buhlmann & van de Geer 2010).
findings.source: Derivation; literature from memory (verify)
findings.relevance: Fit-based competition gives task-dependent case splits, but only local guarantees and extra parts: less elegant, and theorem 0 survives only conditionally.

findings.claim: (b) Nessler et al. 2013: STDP in soft-WTA circuits approximates EM. Weights converge stochastically to the log of a probability (a log conditional probability of the input given the hidden cause), and neuron excitability converges to the log prior. The fixed point is the maximum-likelihood fit of a generative mixture of hidden causes. The weights are conditional means of pre given post (Hebbian averages), with no term that makes synapses of one unit explain each other away (decorrelation). So competition in Nessler's circuit is among hypotheses (units), while in the lasso it is among synapses within one hypothesis. Nessler-STDP has no lasso fixed point; the two are orthogonal axes of competition.
findings.source: Nessler, Pfeiffer, Buesing & Maass 2013, PLoS Comput Biol 9(4):e1003037 (web-checked abstract and text: STDP + excitability adaptation approximates EM; weights converge stochastically to the log of a probability) https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3636028 ; the 'no explaining-away' contrast is our analysis
findings.relevance: Corrects the handoff's phrasing ('lasso and STDP+WTA are two axes'): the two axes are units (WTA/EM, nonconvex) vs synapses (lasso, convex), not explanatory power vs temporal precedence.

findings.claim: Finite-lambda closeness (noiseless demos). Under the irrepresentable condition and sign consistency (min |theta*_S| > lam |G_SS^-1 sign|_inf), the lasso solution is theta_S = theta*_S - lam sign(theta*_S) G_SS^-1 on the true support S and 0 elsewhere. The query read error is -lam phi_S(o*)^T G_SS^-1 sign(theta*_S), so the argmax is exact whenever the query margin exceeds it. Through the kernel proposition this carries over to every kernel variant (lam -> lam/k_h, positive scale k_h/k_a).
findings.source: Numerical check: closed form matches within 1.25e-12 over 20 trials with the condition holding (scratchpad/theory/finite_lam.py); standard result: Fuchs 2004, Zhao & Yu 2006, Wainwright 2009 (from memory, verify)
findings.relevance: Gives the 'provably close' form of theorem 0 at finite lambda (the model uses lambda of about 0.005, not 0+), and it holds for all the fixed-point-preserving STDP variants.

findings.claim: STDP with an LTD-dominated window and hard weight bounds creates competition among synapses onto one neuron and a bimodal (near-sparse) weight distribution, selecting inputs that reliably precede the post spike (Song, Miller & Abbott 2000). STDP + WTA with latency codes concentrates weights on the earliest afferents (Masquelier & Thorpe 2007). Both select by temporal precedence, not by fit, and neither has a regression fixed point.
findings.source: Song, Miller & Abbott 2000, Nat Neurosci; Masquelier & Thorpe 2007, PLoS Comput Biol (from memory, verify)
findings.relevance: Precedence-based synaptic competition exists in the literature but gives an L0-like, nonconvex selection without a theorem-0-type guarantee.

findings.claim: Interpretation (conjecture). design_implications: Keep the code and rewrite the explanation. Present the rule head as a delta-rule synapse: Hebbian with the teacher, anti-Hebbian with its own read, lateral inhibition among synapses with strength G = co-activity of their presynaptic features, plus uniform depression with a floor. State that this is exactly unit-step LCA, whose fixed point is the lasso, so theorem 0 applies unchanged. No new terms are needed: delta rule, LCA, soft-thresholding / proximal L1 and the Dale split are standard names.

Make the fixed-point proposition the theory hinge of the paper. Any two-sided recursion kernel with positive DC gain that is the same for every colour gives the same converged argmax at lambda -> 0+; the odd lobe changes only the path. This lets thesis 1 (STDP generalises Hebb, DC = Hebbian term) and theorem 0 sit in one formalism shared by the bands memory and the rule synapse. Add the finite-lambda closed form for the 'provably close' version.

Use TEM's verified update M <- lambda M + eta (p - p_hat)(p + p_hat)^T as the bridge between the two theses. It is a zero-DC two-time kernel with classical STDP signs over prediction -> observation, and S - theta G is its hetero-associative version. Cite Whittington et al. 2020 STAR Methods.

Do not replace the soft threshold with a hard threshold or k-WTA for the guarantee. With noiseless demos, every exact fit with large enough entries is then a fixed point, selection moves into the start state and path, the guarantee needs RIP_3s instead of the null-space property, and our check recovered the rule less often (0.5 vs 1.0 at n=30). If the paper wants timing to matter for selection, state this convex vs nonconvex trade openly as a limitation or future direction, not as the design.

If rule units or a mixture are added later, gate by perception (a lasso on g (x) phi, group sparsity over experts). It stays convex and theorem 0 holds as stated. Avoid gating by demo fit (EM-style soft-WTA) for the guaranteed path: it gives only local guarantees and needs a second fast synapse to gate the query.

If an odd lobe is ever put on the rule synapse, the theory fixes its form: (i) present the read (prediction) before the observed colour within each step; (ii) make the post-leading lobe LTD-like; (iii) stop the window or gate at the observe event, because a full clamp/release cycle cancels exactly. A constant teacher makes the lobe inert.

In the paper, place the claims that STDP matters where the theory allows them: (a) perception (bands kernels, Sudoku extrapolation, wandering vs locking); (b) nonconvex search (torus three-factor: TD modulator plus soft-WTA); (c) finite-block convergence speed. Do not claim that temporal asymmetry improves rule selection in the convex rule synapse: at convergence it provably cannot.

Correct the handoff's framing that 'lasso and STDP+WTA are two axes (explanatory power / temporal precedence)'. The precise version: WTA/EM (Nessler) is competition among hypotheses (units, maximum likelihood, nonconvex); the lasso/LCA is competition among synapses within a hypothesis (explaining away, convex). Precedence-based STDP competition (Song-Miller-Abbott, Masquelier-Thorpe) gives L0-like selection without a regression fixed point.

A cheap decisive CPU test, if wanted, on the noiseless sparse-regression setting from checks.py: soft vs hard threshold, each with an odd recursion kernel on vs off. Prediction: under the soft threshold the kernel never changes the converged answer; under the hard threshold it changes which fit is chosen. The outcome is a yes/no on the invariance claim. It is not an ARC experiment and costs no GPU.
All of this leaves the hypothesis family unchanged. Keep the ARC-2 condition-S limitation in the paper as it is.
