ground:literature.summary:
Verdict on the user's question (would replacing the lasso make the architecture and the explanation come out elegant?): the literature says the elegant move is to re-describe the lasso and add STDP to it, not to swap it for STDP + WTA.

(1) The rule head's step, theta <- soft(theta - (theta G - S), lam) = soft(S + theta(I - G), lam), is already a discrete locally competitive circuit (Rozell et al. 2008, eq. 3.2, Euler step = tau): S is the feed-forward Hebbian drive (label x feature), G - I is lateral inhibition between features (Gram / co-activation, the Foldiak/SAILnet anti-Hebbian decorrelation), and the soft threshold is constant LTD. LISTA (Gregor & LeCun 2010) calls this mutual inhibition / explaining away. So 'competition' is already in the model, and calling it LCA costs no theorem.

(2) The natural place for STDP is the way G and S are accumulated over recursion time. Xie & Seung (NIPS 1999) show a pairing window reduces to beta0 * (rate Hebb) + beta1 * (pre x d post/dt), and the derivative term vanishes at constant rates. So a learned two-sided kernel on the rule statistics collapses at a fixed point to its DC gain times the present (G, S), and theorem 0 survives at fixed points. With post = y constant (current design) the odd lobe is only a phi-filter. It carries information only if post moves. If the demo cell's own prediction is the post and is nudged toward its label, then by Bengio et al. 2015 and Equilibrium Propagation the odd lobe yields (label - prediction) phi^T = S - theta G, which is the lasso's delta-rule term. That gives one learned kernel for perception and rule synapse: DC = Hebbian, odd = delta rule, constant LTD = threshold. This unification is our inference from verified sources, not a published result.

(3) Hard competition makes things worse, not cleaner. Hard threshold = L0-like, nonconvex, local minima (Rozell's HLCA), and k-WTA = IHT. IHT's guarantee needs a RIP condition (beta_3s < 1/8, rescaled, in the arXiv version). That is stronger than the null-space property and cannot be computed for a given matrix, and Blumensath & Davies themselves report IHT does worse on average than L1 methods. Softmax WTA never gives exact zeros and averages near-equal patterns (Ramsauer's metastable states). Single-winner STDP+WTA (Masquelier & Thorpe, Nessler et al. EM, Diehl & Cook's k-means-like learning) gives one-of-K learned prototypes, and Foldiak 1990 explicitly argues WTA needs one unit per combination ('yellow Volkswagen'), whereas a decorrelated distributed code generalises along single factors. That is bad for ARC's compositional rules. Unsupervised STDP+WTA also picks features that are frequent or early, not diagnostic (Mozafari 2018 needs reward-modulated STDP for that).

(4) None of these competition mechanisms widens the hypothesis family S, which is the ARC-2 failure. The literature that does speak to S is about where competition sits: Maass 2000 (a single soft-WTA over weighted sums is a universal approximator) points to competition in the read, and Kappel et al. 2014 (WTA + lateral STDP learns HMM transitions) points to a transition head.

(5) The three-factor literature explains the torus toy's consolidation failure. Reward-modulated STDP needs a modulator that is zero-mean per task/stimulus (an internal critic), and TD-STDP stops learning once values converge (Fremaux et al. 2010; Fremaux & Gerstner 2016). A fixed baseline b gives delta = -b at the solution.

(6) For the lineage section, verified steps: linear attention = additive fast weights with capacity <= d_dot (Schlag et al. 2021); delta rule = one SGD step on 0.5||Sk - v||^2 (DeltaNet). The rule head is the batch-over-demonstrations delta rule plus a proximal L1 step, iterated over recursion.

Search-level or memory-only items are marked verified=false.

findings.claim: LCA dynamics: u_dot = (1/tau)[b - u - (Phi^T Phi - I) a], a = T_lambda(u), with b = Phi^T s (eq. 3.2). Node m inhibits node n in proportion to a_m G_mn (G = Phi^T Phi), and only above-threshold nodes inhibit, so inhibition is 'usually one-way'. Threshold and cost are linked by lambda dC/da = u - a (eq. 3.4). Soft threshold gives the L1 cost, so SLCA solves BPDN/lasso. Hard threshold gives the cost lambda^2 I(|a| > lambda), which the paper calls 'L0-like'. HLCA is nonconvex, finds only local minima, 'cannot guarantee the L0 sparsest solution', and is not equivalent to matching pursuit.
findings.source: Rozell, Johnson, Baraniuk, Olshausen 2008, Neural Computation 20:2526-2563; https://redwood.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/01/rozell2008sparse.pdf
findings.relevance: Direct mapping, our derivation: the rule head step theta <- soft(theta - (theta G - S), lam) = soft(S + theta(I - G), lam) is the Euler step (dt = tau) of an LCA. b = S (supervised Hebbian label x feature drive), lateral inhibition = G - I (feature Gram), threshold = lambda. There are 13 colour rows, each an LCA, all sharing G. So the rule synapse is already a lateral-inhibition circuit. Swapping in a hard threshold (k-WTA) moves from the convex SLCA to the nonconvex HLCA and loses the global-minimiser part of theorem 0.

findings.claim: ISTA and coordinate descent refine the code through 'a form of mutual inhibition between code components, and component-wise shrinkage'. LISTA ('Learned ISTA') unrolls ISTA, Z(k+1) = h_theta(W_e X + S Z(k)), and learns W_e and S for a fixed number of iterations. It gives an approximate 'explaining away (or competition)' and about 10x less computation than Li & Osher's coordinate descent at equal error.
findings.source: Gregor & LeCun 2010, ICML, Learning Fast Approximations of Sparse Coding; https://gwern.net/doc/ai/nn/retrieval/2010-gregor.pdf
findings.relevance: The rule head (fixed block count, learned lambda) is a LISTA-style unrolled ISTA. The existing literature already calls the theta G term 'competition / explaining away', so the paper can describe it as competition without a new term. A kernel-accumulated G is a further learned version of LISTA's S matrix.

findings.claim: Foldiak's network has Hebbian feed-forward units with anti-Hebbian lateral feedback. Rules: lateral Delta w_ij = -alpha(y_i y_j - p^2); feed-forward Delta q_ij = beta y_i (x_j - q_ij); threshold Delta t_i = gamma(y_i - p), with p the target bit probability. 'Provided that the feedback is symmetric (w_ij = w_ji), the network is guaranteed to settle into a stable state' (Hopfield 1982). The paper contrasts this with WTA: competitive learning would need a separate unit per combination ('yellow Volkswagen detector'), whereas decorrelated units can code colour and type separately and generalise along one feature. The resulting sparse code is described as favourable input to a later supervised associative layer.
findings.source: Foldiak 1990, Biological Cybernetics 64:165-170; https://redwood.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/foldiak90.pdf
findings.relevance: The theta G term is the analogue of Foldiak's anti-Hebbian decorrelation, and adaptive thresholds are the analogue of lambda. Foldiak's own argument against WTA is the main literature reason a single-winner rule synapse would hurt ARC: ARC rules are factorial (colour map x position map). The symmetric-feedback condition warns that asymmetric (STDP) lateral weights lose the settling guarantee.

findings.claim: SAILnet rules: Delta W_im = alpha(n_i n_m - p^2), Delta Q_ik = beta n_i (X_k - n_i Q_ik) (Oja), Delta theta_i = gamma(n_i - p). They come from gradient descent on a Lagrangian: reconstruction error + sum_i lambda_i(n_i - p) + sum tau_im(n_i n_m - p^2). Thresholds and inhibitory weights correspond to the Lagrange multipliers (lambda_i ~ -theta_i, tau_im ~ -W_im). Oja's local rule approximates the non-local gradient only 'in the limit that the neuronal activity is sparse and uncorrelated'. Integer spike counts at p = 0.05 give 'hard', or L0, sparseness.
findings.source: Zylberberg, Murphy, DeWeese 2011, PLoS Comput Biol 7(10):e1002250; https://arxiv.org/pdf/1109.2239
findings.relevance: A principled replacement for the hand-set lambda ~ kappa/sqrt(n): a threshold that is the Lagrange multiplier of a target support size (homeostasis). This gives k-WTA-like sparsity control while keeping a soft-threshold step. It also shows that sparseness plus decorrelation is what makes local Hebbian rules valid gradient steps, which is a reason to keep the decorrelating G term.

findings.claim: In sparse coding with an overcomplete basis, the coefficients a_i come from the equilibrium of a recurrent computation. The residual image is fed forward through phi_i, and each a_i is self-inhibited by S'(a_i), an analysis-synthesis loop (Mumford 1994). Learning is 'a Hebbian update of the phi_i based on the average joint activity between the outputs (a_i) and the residual image'. Overlapping bases compete, which makes the input-output map nonlinear.
findings.source: Olshausen & Field 1997, Vision Research 37(23):3311-3325; https://boulderschool.yale.edu/sites/default/files/files/Olshausen_Field_1997.pdf (1996 Nature 381:607-609 seen only at abstract level)
findings.relevance: Origin of 'inference = recurrent explaining-away; learning = Hebbian on output x residual (an error-times-pre delta form)'. That is the same split as the rule head (fast theta inference) vs slow W_phi learning.

findings.claim: IHT: y[n+1] = H_s(y[n] + Phi^T(x - Phi y[n])), where H_s keeps the s largest-magnitude entries. The theorem uses a rescaled RIP constant beta_s. If beta_3s < 1/8, every iteration reduces the error, and the result comes within a constant factor (6 * epsilon) of the best attainable error in about log2(SNR) iterations. Convergence alone holds when ||Phi||_2 < 1. RIP cannot in general be computed for a given matrix ('none of the above is possible in general'); only random constructions are known to satisfy it. Section VII: IHT 'does also perform less well in numerical studies than CoSaMP or l1 based approaches'.
findings.source: Blumensath & Davies, Iterative Hard Thresholding for Compressed Sensing, arXiv:0805.0510 v1 (journal version ACHA 27(3):265-274, 2009, and its constant delta_3s < 1/sqrt(32), are from memory: NOT verified)
findings.relevance: k-WTA in the rule synapse is IHT. Theorem 0's identification condition (I) would change from the null-space property, which is necessary and sufficient for L1, to a RIP_3s condition, which is sufficient only, stronger, and not certifiable for a learned demo code. The convex convergence condition (C) becomes a local one. Average-case behaviour is also worse. Net: a weaker theorem and a less clean story.

findings.claim: The null-space property is a necessary and sufficient condition: every s-sparse solution of min ||x||_1 s.t. y = Theta x is the unique solution iff for all h in ker(Theta) \ {0} and all |S| <= s, ||h_S||_1 < ||h_{S^c}||_1. It is called a 'classic result' and contrasted with RIP and coherence, which are sufficient only.
findings.source: Stated as a classic result in arXiv:2304.05526 (Necessary and Sufficient Conditions for Simultaneous State and Input Recovery ... by l1-Minimization). Original attribution (Donoho & Huo 2001; Gribonval & Nielsen 2003; Cohen, Dahmen, DeVore 2009) is from memory, NOT verified.
findings.relevance: Confirms that theorem 0's (I) is the tight (iff) condition only for L1. Moving to L0/k-WTA gives up the iff.

findings.claim: Spark(A) is the smallest number of linearly dependent columns. A representation with ||gamma||_0 < Spark/2 is necessarily the sparsest. If the off-diagonal Gram entries are bounded by M and ||gamma_0||_0 < (1 + 1/M)/2, then gamma_0 is the unique L1 solution.
findings.source: Donoho & Elad 2003, PNAS 100(5):2197-2202; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC153464
findings.relevance: The L0 minimiser is unique under the spark condition, but finding it is combinatorial. A coherence bound on the demo Gram G is a checkable, if weak, sufficient condition for theorem 0 that could be logged per task.

findings.claim: The k-sparse autoencoder keeps only the k largest hidden activations. The paper analyses it as iterative thresholding with inversion (Maleki 2009, an IHT variant): support estimation keeps the k largest entries of the back-projected residual, then a least-squares inversion step follows. Recovery is argued under dictionary incoherence (mutual coherence).
findings.source: Makhzani & Frey, k-Sparse Autoencoders, arXiv:1312.5663 (ICLR 2014 per DBLP); https://arxiv.org/pdf/1312.5663
findings.relevance: Establishes k-WTA = one hard-thresholding (support-selection) step in published deep-learning terms. It can be cited for 'k-WTA = L0 projection' rather than claiming it. That H_s is the Euclidean projection onto the s-sparse set is standard math, not separately sourced.

findings.claim: sparsemax(z) := argmin over p in the simplex of ||p - z||^2, the Euclidean projection onto the probability simplex. Its solution is sparsemax_i(z) = [z_i - tau(z)]_+, where tau is the unique threshold with sum_j [z_j - tau]_+ = 1. That is, 'such projections correspond to a soft-thresholding operation'.
findings.source: Martins & Astudillo 2016, From Softmax to Sparsemax, arXiv:1602.02068 (ICML 2016, venue from memory)
findings.relevance: The exact bridge between a WTA-style normalised competition and the soft threshold: 'soft-threshold with an adaptive threshold' is sparsemax. On the simplex ||p||_1 = 1 is constant (trivial), so the selection principle becomes nearest-point projection rather than minimum L1. Usable for frame or read selection while keeping exact zeros; softmax never gives zeros.

findings.claim: Masquelier & Thorpe use an S1-C1-S2-C2 hierarchy with time-to-first-spike (rank-order) coding and at most one spike per neuron per image. 'A one-winner-take-all mechanism prevents the other duplicated cells from firing'. During learning they add local inhibition and a k-WTA (at most two cells per scale). STDP is simplified: the change depends only on the sign of t_i - t_j, with an infinite window, soft bounds w(1 - w), and depression of synapses that got no spike. S2 learns 'intermediate-complexity' features: afferent clusters that consistently fire earliest (face and motorbike parts). With 20 features, accuracy is 95.0% (binary + RBF) and 97.7% (potential + RBF) on faces/motorbikes/background.
findings.source: Masquelier & Thorpe 2007, PLoS Comput Biol 3(2):e31; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1797822
findings.relevance: Canonical 'latency code + STDP + WTA'. What it learns is what is repeated and early, not what is consistent with a set of labelled pairs. Used as a rule synapse, it would latch onto the earliest or most frequent feature-label coincidence across demos rather than the rule that explains all demos.

findings.claim: Nessler et al. 2013 use a soft WTA with common lateral inhibition, and each output spike is a sample from the posterior over hidden causes. STDP is Delta w_ki = c e^{-w_ki} - 1 if the presynaptic neuron fired in [t_f - sigma, t_f], and -1 otherwise (eq. 5). Its equilibrium is w_ki = log p*(y_i = 1 | z_k = 1) + log c (eq. 6). Intrinsic excitability Delta w_k0 = e^{-w_k0} z_k - 1 converges to log p*(z_k = 1), the prior. The inputs are population-coded (exactly one active neuron per group), and normalisation holds only approximately. Theorem 1: the weights converge with probability 1 to the set of local maxima of the likelihood (stochastic approximation, online EM).
findings.source: Nessler, Pfeiffer, Buesing, Maass 2013, PLoS Comput Biol 9(4):e1003037; https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article/file?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003037&type=printable
findings.relevance: Gives an STDP+WTA rule synapse a rigorous Bayesian reading: the hypothesis family is a mixture of K learned causes (rule prototypes), and selection is posterior sampling with a learned log-prior (excitability, a code-length analogue). This parallels the old doc's reading of the lasso as Laplace-prior MAP. But it is discrete one-of-K and reaches only local maxima, and the fixed -1 depression is the same role as the lasso's constant LTD.

findings.claim: Diehl & Cook use Poisson inputs to excitatory neurons, each paired one-to-one with an inhibitory neuron that inhibits all other excitatory neurons (lateral-inhibition WTA). Each neuron's adaptive threshold theta rises at every spike and decays. They test four STDP variants with similar results. Training is unsupervised, and labels are assigned post hoc (each neuron gets its best-responding class). MNIST accuracy: 82.9% (400), 87.0% (1600), 95.0% (6400 neurons). The authors call it 'similar to competitive learning procedures' that 'share aspects with k-means'.
findings.source: Diehl & Cook 2015, Front Comput Neurosci 9:99; https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/computational-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fncom.2015.00099/full
findings.relevance: STDP + WTA + homeostatic threshold behaves like prototype clustering and needs thousands of units for 95% on MNIST. As a rule mechanism it is a library of stored rules, not per-task inference from 2-4 demos. Homeostasis is essential, the same role as lambda calibration.

findings.claim: Reward-modulated STDP (R-STDP) with first-spike WTA readout: the first output neuron to fire is the decision. Reward applies STDP to the winner and punishment applies anti-STDP. 'Classic unsupervised STDP extracts any feature that consistently repeats', whereas R-STDP extracts discriminative ones. Reported accuracy for R-STDP vs STDP: about 98.9 vs 97.2% (Caltech face/motorbike), 89.5 vs 84.5% (ETH-80), 88.4 vs about 66% (NORB).
findings.source: Mozafari, Kheradpisheh, Masquelier, Nowzari-Dalini, Ganjtabesh 2018, IEEE TNNLS 29(12) (venue from catalogue); https://ar5iv.arxiv.org/html/1705.09132
findings.relevance: Supervised and rule-like learning with STDP+WTA needs a third factor. For the rule synapse that factor would be demonstration consistency (as in the torus toy), not plain STDP.

findings.claim: Three-factor rules take the form w_dot = F(M, pre, post), e.g. w_dot = M e with eligibility trace e_dot = -e/tau_e + STDP(pre, post). R-STDP is w_dot = (R - b) e. The covariance form 'can function properly only if the neuromodulatory signal M is zero on average', and the expected change is Cov(R, H(pre, post)). TD-STDP, w_dot = delta_TD H(pre, post), stops learning once state values converge. R-max follows from policy gradient.
findings.source: Fremaux & Gerstner 2016, Front Neural Circuits 9:85; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4717313/
findings.relevance: Gives the torus toy's dopamine delta = Delta consistency - b its standard name (three-factor R-STDP with eligibility trace), so no new term is needed. TD-STDP's property that learning stops at convergence is exactly the consolidation behaviour the toy lacked.

findings.claim: All reward-modulated Hebbian rules split into a reward-covariance term and an unsupervised term. They work 'only if the expected reward is calculated for each task and stimulus separately'. 'If several tasks are to be learned simultaneously, the nervous system needs an internal critic'. 'R-STDP, but not R-max, needs a stimulus-specific reward-prediction system'.
findings.source: Fremaux, Sprekeler, Gerstner 2010, J Neurosci 30(40):13326-13337; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6634722
findings.relevance: A literature-backed diagnosis of the toy's consolidation failure. A fixed baseline b = 0.2 is not a task- or state-specific reward prediction, so staying at the solution gets delta = -b. The fix is a per-task critic (expected consistency) or a TD error, not a new mechanism.

findings.claim: Gerstner et al. 2018 review four experiments supporting synaptic eligibility traces lasting seconds, combined with a third factor, as the substrate of neoHebbian three-factor rules.
findings.source: Gerstner, Lehmann, Liakoni, Corneil, Brea 2018, Front Neural Circuits 12:53 (abstract only, via search)
findings.relevance: Biological support for keeping a trace (kappa) term. Note the torus toy found the trace added little; this source does not contradict that.

findings.claim: Backpropamine: x_j(t) = sigma(sum_i (w_ij + alpha_ij Hebb_ij) x_i(t-1)). The plain rule is Hebb_ij(t+1) = Clip(Hebb_ij + eta x_i(t-1) x_j(t)). Neuromodulated: Hebb += M(t) x_i(t-1) x_j(t), with M(t) computed by the network. Retroactive: Hebb += M(t) E_ij, with E_ij(t+1) = (1 - eta) E_ij + eta x_i(t-1) x_j(t), an eligibility trace with trainable decay. Everything is trained by backpropagation. Tasks: cue-reward association, a 9x9 maze, and PTB language modelling. Retroactive modulation gives about 1.7 perplexity over the baseline LSTM (p = 1e-7), and the gain over simple modulation is not significant (p = 0.066). The paper flags 'interference between the unsupervised component of Hebbian learning and reward-based modifications' (citing Fremaux et al. 2010).
findings.source: Miconi, Rawal, Clune, Stanley, ICLR 2019; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.10585
findings.relevance: The closest precedent. Its pairing x_i(t-1) x_j(t) is a one-lag causal kernel plus an exponential trace over sequence time. The differences to claim: a learned two-sided multi-band kernel over recursion depth, and a selection principle (soft-threshold competition with theorem 0). Do not claim learned neuromodulated plasticity as new.

findings.claim: Under rate approximations, an STDP pairing function f gives Delta W ~ beta0 nu_i nu_j + beta1 nu_i_dot nu_j, with beta0 = integral of f and beta1 = first moment of f (eq. 6-7). When the lobes cancel (beta0 = 0), plasticity depends only on the derivative of the postsynaptic rate ('differential Hebbian / anti-Hebbian'), and 'a constant postsynaptic firing rate causes no net change'.
findings.source: Xie & Seung, Spike-based Learning Rules and Stabilization of Persistent Neural Activity, NIPS 12 (1999/2000); https://papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/1999/file/c0560792e4a3c79e62f76cbf9fb277dd-Paper.pdf
findings.relevance: The primary citation for the paper's thesis, without coining a term: the DC part of the kernel is the Hebbian term and the odd part encodes the trajectory and vanishes at fixed points. For the rule synapse, the kernel-accumulated statistics reduce at a fixed point to beta0 * (G, S), so theorem 0 still applies there (with lambda scaled by beta0).

findings.claim: Bengio et al. propose Delta W_ij ~ s_i_dot rho(s_j): presynaptic rate times the rate of change of postsynaptic activity, consistent with STDP. If the dynamics move activity to reduce an objective J (dJ/ds_i ~ s_i_dot), this rule is stochastic gradient descent on J. They credit the idea to Xie & Seung (2000) and Hinton (2007).
findings.source: Bengio, Mesnard, Fischer, Zhang, Wu, STDP as presynaptic activity times rate of change of postsynaptic activity, arXiv:1509.05936
findings.relevance: Key to an elegant rule synapse. If the post for a demo output cell is its own prediction moving toward its label, the odd lobe of a learned kernel yields (label - prediction) phi^T = S - theta G, which is the lasso's gradient term. The delta-rule part of the step would then come from the STDP kernel itself (our inference).

findings.claim: Equilibrium Propagation: a second phase nudges the network's fixed point toward lower prediction error, and the propagated perturbation encodes the gradient. This holds when synaptic updates follow a standard STDP-like rule. The paper relates the method to Contrastive Hebbian Learning.
findings.source: Scellier & Bengio 2017, Front Comput Neurosci 11:24; https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.05179 (abstract)
findings.relevance: A second precedent that 'Hebbian difference between free and nudged states = gradient'. The rule head's theta G - S is exactly Hebb(prediction, phi) - Hebb(label, phi), a contrastive Hebbian form. Xie & Seung 2003 (backprop = contrastive Hebbian) is from memory, NOT verified.

findings.claim: Stable competitive STDP needs the integral of the window F to be negative (A- tau- > A+ tau+), 'which ensures that uncorrelated pre- and postsynaptic spikes produce an overall weakening of synapses'. They use A-/A+ = 1.05. Inputs with short latency or in correlated groups win, and others weaken, without global signals or preset activity levels.
findings.source: Song, Miller, Abbott 2000, Nature Neuroscience 3(9):919-926; https://www.dam.brown.edu/people/elie/NEUR_1680_2012/Song_Miller_Abbott_2000.pdf
findings.relevance: Competition among synapses arises from net LTD of the kernel. This ties together three formalisms: the lasso's constant LTD (soft threshold), Nessler's fixed -1 depression, and the Sudoku finding that 7/8 heads drive the fixed-point Hebbian gain to zero or below. It is the literature anchor for 'competition = net LTD'.

findings.claim: A single soft-WTA unit applied to weighted sums of inputs can approximate any continuous function, and a single k-WTA unit can compute any Boolean function of weighted sums. Positive weights suffice. A multi-layer perceptron needs quadratically many gates to compute WTA over n inputs.
findings.source: Maass, Neural Computation with Winner-Take-All as the Only Nonlinear Operation, NIPS 1999 (abstract); also Maass 2000, Neural Computation 12(11):2519-2535 (bibliographic only)
findings.relevance: The one result here that bears on the hypothesis family S. Competition in the read (output cell = WTA over weighted template matches, i.e. conditional or pointer-like rules) adds expressivity. A threshold on theta does not. The universality uses slow-learned weights, so per-task identification from demos is not covered.

findings.claim: In a WTA circuit with lateral excitatory synapses under STDP, temporal context is encoded in the lateral synapses ('each neuron has learned to fire after a distinct set of predecessors'), which act as the HMM transition model, and feed-forward synapses act as the emission model. This approximates online EM for HMMs via forward sampling. The authors report that 'the full power of hidden Markov model learning can be attained through reward-gated STDP' (rejection sampling). Demonstrations include sequence memory and replay and artificial grammar learning.
findings.source: Kappel, Nessler, Maass 2014, PLoS Comput Biol 10(3):e1003511; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3967926
findings.relevance: Direct precedent for the planned transition head (phi(t) -> phi(t+1) solved from demo trajectories). That is where a temporally asymmetric kernel and WTA have a real job (post changes), and it is the path toward procedural rules (S).

findings.claim: Modern Hopfield network: energy E = -lse(beta, X^T xi) + 0.5 xi^T xi + ..., update xi_new = X softmax(beta X^T xi), which equals transformer attention. Global convergence to stationary points follows via CCCP (Theorems 1-2). Storage is exponential in dimension (Theorem 3). Retrieval error after one update is exponentially small in the separation Delta_i = x_i^T x_i - max_j x_i^T x_j (Theorems 4-5). Similar patterns produce metastable states that average a subset, and with no separation the iteration converges to a global fixed point near the mean.
findings.source: Ramsauer et al. 2020/ICLR 2021, Hopfield Networks is All You Need, arXiv:2008.02217
findings.relevance: The frames kappa_k are already soft-WTA (Hopfield) reads. A softmax WTA over candidate rules would average near-equally consistent hypotheses (metastable) instead of choosing the sparsest. So softmax is the wrong replacement for the lasso's selection principle, but it is fine for retrieval of well-separated candidates.

findings.claim: Linearised self-attention equals a fast weight programmer: W^(i) = W^(i-1) + v^(i) (outer) phi(k^(i)) (Sec. 3.2, eq. 17). Keys in d_dot dimensions allow at most d_dot orthogonal keys, and storing more 'will result in a retrieval error'. Fix: the delta rule W^(i) = W^(i-1) + beta^(i)(v^(i) - W^(i-1) phi(k^(i))) (outer) phi(k^(i)), with beta = sigma(W_beta x), plus sum normalisation of phi.
findings.source: Schlag, Irie, Schmidhuber 2021, ICML, Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers; https://arxiv.org/html/2102.11174v3
findings.relevance: Verified first step of the paper's lineage (Hebbian outer product -> fast weight -> linear attention -> delta rule). The bands memory is the additive, gated Hebbian form. The rule head's theta G - S is the batch-over-demos delta-rule error.

findings.claim: DeltaNet: S_t = S_{t-1} - beta_t(S_{t-1} k_t - v_t) k_t^T, i.e. one SGD step on L_t = 0.5||S k_t - v_t||^2, equivalently S_{t-1}(I - beta_t k_t k_t^T) + beta_t v_t k_t^T (a generalised Householder transition). The paper gives a WY-representation parallel algorithm. A 1.3B model on 100B tokens beats Mamba and GLA on perplexity and zero-shot tasks.
findings.source: Yang, Wang, Zhang, Shen, Kim 2024, NeurIPS, Parallelizing Linear Transformers with the Delta Rule over Sequence Length; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.06484
findings.relevance: The rule head is DeltaNet's regression solved over the demo set (batch, leave-one-out) with a proximal L1 step, iterated over recursion. That gives the lineage a clean statement (online regression -> regularised regression over demos). Gated DeltaNet (Yang, Kautz, Hatamizadeh, ICLR 2025: gating + delta) was seen only at search level, NOT verified.

findings.claim: Associative memory over tokens equals regression at test time. Architectures (linear attention, gated variants, SSMs, online learners, softmax attention) are specified by the association weighting, the regressor class, and the test-time optimiser.
findings.source: Wang, Shi, Fox, Test-time regression, arXiv:2501.12352 (search-level only; JMLR listing seen in search)
findings.relevance: If confirmed, a ready-made frame for the rule head: weighting = leave-one-out demo cells, regressor = linear on phi + frames, optimiser = proximal gradient with L1. Needs to be read before citing.

findings.claim: Under teacher forcing (output clamped to the target), STDP has no perceptron-style convergence guarantee for arbitrary spike inputs. Average-case versions hold for Poisson inputs, where learnability reduces to linear separability (applied to the columns of the input correlation matrix).
findings.source: Legenstein, Naeger, Maass 2005, Neural Computation 17(11) (abstract page https://igi-web.tugraz.at/people/Abstracts/LegensteinETAL:04)
findings.relevance: Supervised STDP inherits a linear-separability hypothesis class and loses worst-case guarantees. This is literature support that an STDP rule synapse would neither widen S nor strengthen theorem 0.

findings.claim: Hebbian/anti-Hebbian networks derived from similarity-matching objectives give local-rule sparse dictionary learning with the Olshausen-Field architecture. Krotov & Hopfield 2019 learn features with local Hebbian-like rules under global hidden-layer inhibition.
findings.source: Hu, Pehlevan, Chklovskii 2014 (arXiv:1503.00690); Krotov & Hopfield 2019, PNAS 116(16):7723-7731 (both search-level only)
findings.relevance: Optional citations showing that lateral-inhibition Hebbian circuits can be derived from objectives (normative). Not needed for the core argument.

design_implications: Keep the soft-threshold step and describe it as competition. With step 1, theta <- soft(S + theta(I - G), lam) is the Euler step of Rozell's LCA: b = S (supervised Hebbian label x feature drive), lateral inhibition = G - I (anti-Hebbian decorrelation in Foldiak's sense), lam = constant LTD. LISTA calls this 'mutual inhibition / explaining away'. The paper can then say the rule synapse is a locally competitive circuit over hypothesis coefficients with no new mechanism and no new term, and theorem 0 stays exact (NSP is iff for L1).

Use STDP for accumulating the statistics over recursion, not as a substitute for the selection principle. By Xie & Seung, a learned two-sided kernel K on the rule statistics reduces to beta0 * (G, S) at a fixed point (the odd lobe vanishes), so theorem 0 holds at fixed points with lambda effectively scaled by beta0. That gives one learned kernel in perception and rule synapse: DC lobe = Hebbian statistics, odd lobe = trajectory.

Make the odd lobe carry information by changing the post. With post = y constant (current design), the asymmetric kernel only filters phi. Use the demo output cell's own prediction (theta phi, or the fed-back read) as the post and let it be nudged toward its label over blocks. Then, by Bengio et al. 2015 and Equilibrium Propagation, the odd lobe gives (label - prediction) phi^T = S - theta G, the lasso's gradient term. The proximal step becomes 'STDP odd lobe + constant LTD floor'. This is the most elegant unification the literature supports. It is our inference; test it as a binary from-scratch intervention, not as a graded knob.

Keep the interaction matrix symmetric. Settling and energy guarantees (Hopfield/Foldiak's symmetric-feedback condition, LCA's energy on Phi^T Phi, Ramsauer's CCCP) need symmetric interactions. Suggested rule: build G from the DC (symmetric) part of the kernel and let only S see the full asymmetric kernel. Convergence (C) is then kept, and direction sensitivity enters through the drive.

Do not replace the soft threshold with hard k-WTA. That gives HLCA/IHT: nonconvex with local minima, and a uniform guarantee only under RIP_3s (beta_3s < 1/8, rescaled), which is stronger than NSP, sufficient only, and not certifiable for a learned demo code. Blumensath & Davies report IHT is worse than L1 on average. Theorem 0's (I) and (C) both weaken, so the explanation gets less clean.

If a fixed sparsity budget is wanted (to remove the hand-set lambda = kappa/sqrt(n)), use a homeostatic threshold: Foldiak's Delta t = gamma(y - p), SAILnet's thresholds as Lagrange multipliers of a target firing rate, Diehl & Cook's adaptive theta. Lambda becomes the multiplier of a target support size while the step stays soft-threshold (convex). Sparsemax is the principled 'WTA with adaptive threshold' if a normalised selection is needed somewhere.

Do not make the rule synapse a single-winner WTA over rules. Nessler (online EM for mixtures), Diehl & Cook (k-means-like) and Masquelier (earliest repeated pattern) all give one-of-K learned prototypes. Foldiak's own argument says WTA needs one unit per combination, whereas decorrelated codes generalise along single factors. ARC rules are compositional (colour x position x frame), so a one-winner rule synapse shrinks effective S. Unsupervised STDP+WTA also picks frequent or early coincidences, not diagnostic ones (Mozafari: reward-modulated STDP is needed).

Do not present any competition swap as an ARC-2 fix. Lasso, LCA, IHT and the WTA mixture all select among linear-in-feature hypotheses, and ARC-2's 0/172 is an S failure. The literature that bears on S says where to put competition: in the read (Maass 2000: one soft-WTA over weighted sums is universal; the frames kappa already are soft-WTA/Hopfield reads), and in a transition head with lateral STDP inside a WTA (Kappel et al. 2014: transitions in lateral synapses, approximately an HMM). The transition head is where the asymmetric kernel has a real job, since the post changes over time.

For the search/consolidation story, use the standard three-factor form w_dot = (R - b) e with a task-specific critic or TD error (Fremaux et al. 2010; Fremaux & Gerstner 2016). The torus toy's fixed b = 0.2 is exactly the documented failure mode: no stimulus-specific reward prediction, so staying at the solution gets delta = -b. A per-task expected-consistency critic, or a TD-style delta that is zero once consistency stops changing, is the literature fix. Cite it rather than presenting it as new.

Lineage paragraph (mostly verified): Hebbian outer product = linear attention = fast weight programmer with capacity <= d_dot (Schlag 2021) -> delta rule = one SGD step on 0.5||Sk - v||^2 (Schlag; DeltaNet) -> rule head = the same regression solved over the demonstration set with a proximal L1 step (ISTA/LCA), iterated over recursion depth (our statement; Test-time regression framing still unverified) -> learned two-sided kernel over recursion whose DC part is Hebb and whose odd part is the differential (pre x d post/dt) term (Xie & Seung; Bengio et al.). Name Backpropamine (one-lag causal Hebbian trace + eligibility trace + learned modulator, small PTB gains) as the closest precedent, and claim only the two-sided multi-band kernel over recursion depth plus the selection principle as the difference.

Tie 'competition = net LTD' across formalisms as one sentence: Song, Miller & Abbott need a negative integral of the STDP window for stable competition, Nessler's rule has a fixed -1 depression, and the lasso has constant shrinkage lambda. The Sudoku result (7/8 heads with fixed-point Hebbian gain <= 0) can be placed in this line without inventing a term.

design:expressivity-for-ARC-2.name: Free/clamped delta-rule heads under soft WTA: a TEM-style rule synapse (no lasso)
design:expressivity-for-ARC-2.one_sentence: Each demonstration runs through the same perception twice: free (exactly as the query must) and clamped (its answer visible). M rule heads compete for each output cell by soft WTA, so the key is a conjunctive code (role ⊗ φ). At every recursion step the heads bind this code to the observed targets (content rows = colour, transition rows = the clamped code) with the delta rule, which is the predict→observe form of an asymmetric pairing window and needs no threshold. The query reads back the state it would be in if it saw its answer, so the recursion runs a procedure whose update is solved from the demonstrations, and proposition 4 still holds.
design:expressivity-for-ARC-2.equations:
Notation follows arc/model.py.
- L lanes; O = C^2 output-canvas cells; V = 13 (VOCAB); p = cfg.phi (64); M = cfg.rule_heads (4); F = frames + 1 (9); J = cfg.rule_iters (4).
- others [L,L], w = m * demo [L,O] and n = clamp(others @ w.sum(-1), 1), exactly as in statistics().
- unit(x) = x / (|x| + 1e-6); sg = detach.

0. INPUTS
- Free input x: as now (the output canvas is UNKNOWN in every lane).
- Clamped twin of lane l: xc_l = x_l on the input canvas. On the output canvas:
  - xc_l(o) = label_l(o) if demo_l and label_l(o) != PAD (colours 2..11, EOS 12);
  - xc_l(o) = PAD if demo_l and label_l(o) == PAD;
  - xc_l(o) = x_l(o) if not demo_l.
- So test labels never enter xc.

1. PERCEPTION. Blocks t = 1..blocks. Both streams use the same weights, and lanes never mix.
- free: (h_t, ek, ev, w) = block_step(h_{t-1}, emb(x), fb_t), with fb_t = W_fb rc_{t-1} + W_fv rv_{t-1}.
  - W_fb: V -> d (as now). W_fv: p -> d (new). Both zero-initialised.
- clamped: (hc_t, ekc, evc, wc) = block_step(hc_{t-1}, emb(xc), None). There is no feedback, so the observed state depends only on its own pair.
- Bands inside block_step are unchanged:
  - E_K,r <- z_r E_K,r + gamma_r k~
  - D_V,r = z_r E_V,r
  - E_V,r <- D_V,r + gamma_r v
  - S_b = sum_r Re(a_r v^T E_K,r + b_r D_V,r^T k~)
  - W <- (1-eta) W + eta S_b
  - read = q~ (v^T k~ + W)^T

2. CODES on the output cells o
- phi_t(o) = unit(W_phi h_t(o)) in R^p. This is the free key, as features() computes it now.
- pi_t(o) = softmax_m(beta (W_pi h_t(o))_m) in the M-simplex, with beta = softplus(beta_raw). This is the soft WTA among the M head units of a cell.
  - Optional straight-through version: pi <- onehot(argmax pi) + pi - sg(pi).
- psi_t(o) = vec(pi_t(o) (x) phi_t(o)) in R^{Mp}, with |psi| = |pi|_2 |phi| <= 1, so tr G <= 1.
- phic_t(o) = unit(W_phi hc_t(o)) in R^p. This is the clamped code, computed with the same projection.
- Y_t(o) = [ y(o) ; phic_t(o) ] in R^{V+p}.
  - Content rows: the observed colour.
  - Transition rows: the observed code.
- kappa_t,k(o) in R^V is computed as in frame_colours() (k = 0..K). Padding it with p zero rows gives kbar_t,k(o) in R^{V+p}.

3. LEAVE-ONE-OUT STATISTICS. Same machinery: P is computed per lane over its own cells, then others@P/n.
- G_t = others @ [sum_o w psi psi^T] / n, shape [L, Mp, Mp]
- S_t = others @ [sum_o w Y psi^T] / n, shape [L, V+p, Mp]
- C_t,k = others @ [sum_o w kbar_k psi^T] / n, shape [L, F, V+p, Mp]
- H_t,kj = others @ [sum_o w <kappa_k, kappa_j>] / n
- s_t,k = others @ [sum_o w <kappa_k, y>] / n

4. WRITE. Theta [L, V+p, Mp] and Gamma [L, F] are warm-started from the previous block, and the step sizes are detached.
- lhat = Rayleigh quotient of G_t after 8 power iterations from 1/sqrt(Mp) (no gradient, floored at 1e-6).
- eta = 0.9 / lhat; eta_G = 0.9 / lhat(H_t).
- Repeat J times:
  - Theta <- Theta - eta (Theta G_t - S_t + sum_k Gamma_k C_t,k)
  - Gamma_k <- Gamma_k - eta_G ( <Theta, C_t,k>_F + (H_t Gamma)_k - s_t,k )
- Cell form of the Theta step: Theta <- Theta + (eta/n) sum_{l' in others} sum_o w (Y(o) - rhat(o)) psi(o)^T, where rhat = Theta psi + sum_k Gamma_k kbar_k is the head's prediction, read before the write.
  - The Hebbian drive +eta S moves Theta toward the observed association Y psi^T (LTP-like).
  - The anti-Hebbian term -eta Theta G moves it away from the predicted association rhat psi^T (LTD-like). This is lateral inhibition among synapses.
  - Its off-diagonal blocks G[m,m'] = sum pi_m pi_m' phi phi^T / n are inhibition between heads that share cells.
- There is no soft-threshold step, and lam_raw is removed.

5. READ AND OUTPUT
- r_t(o) = Theta psi_t(o) + sum_k Gamma_k kbar_t,k(o) in R^{V+p}.
  - rc = r[:V] is the colour read; rv = r[V:] is the code read.
- Next block's output-canvas injection: emb_out + W_fb rc_t + W_fv rv_t. Through this, the task steers perception.
- logits = classifier(h_T) + tau rc_T (direct_head).
  - With out_ffn: logits = classifier(FFN(RMSNorm(h_T + sqrt(d)(W_fb rc_T + W_fv rv_T)))).

6. CARRY
- {h, ek, ev, w} for 2L lanes (L free lanes plus L clamped twins).
- At a fresh carry: Theta = 0, Gamma = 0, r = 0 [L, O, V+p].
- Detached at segment boundaries and at the first gradient block, as now.

7. REDUCTION. With M = 1, transition rows off (Y = y, no clamped stream, no W_fv), J = 1 and eta = 1, this is exactly today's head at lam = 0 (soft(x, 0) = x).

8. STDP READING OF STEP 4
- In each block the post goes from rhat (prediction) to Y (observation) while the pre psi is fixed.
- A pairing window with an LTD-like post-leading lobe turns this change into a positive multiple of (Y - rhat) psi^T, i.e. the delta rule (Xie & Seung 2000; Bengio et al. 2015). The window must stop at the observation event.
- Filtering S and G with any recursion kernel of DC gains k_h, k_a > 0 changes only the transient. The limit is (k_h/k_a) times the same fit.

9. CHECKS (float64; script at /tmp/claude-0/-workspace-arc1-coupled/ae142cb7-3355-47e0-b126-2adf442a38bb/scratchpad/theory_wta/checks_wta.py)
- Landweber from 0 reaches the min-norm least-squares fit and never leaves the span of the demonstration codes: error 3.8e-11.
- The query error is exactly -Theta*(I - P_D) psi*(o): 3.5e-14.
- Hard gates make G block-diagonal, and the joint fit equals M separate per-head fits: 1.4e-14.
- DC gains (k_h on S, k_a on G) give (k_h/k_a) times the min-norm fit, argmax unchanged: 2.6e-10.
- T steps equal the spectral filter (1-(1-eta s)^T)/s: 4.8e-15. The norm is bounded: |Theta_T| <= T eta |S|.
- At p = 64, M = 4, the step 1/lmax is about 55x larger than the tr G bound, so the power-iteration step is required.

replaces_lasso.lasso_function: Selection principle: among the Theta consistent with the demonstrations, pick the minimum-l1 one (the 'shortest description').
replaces_lasso.replacement: Minimum-norm least squares on a code made sparse by competition. Landweber/delta iteration from Theta = 0 never leaves the span of the demonstration codes, so its limit is the min-norm fit (a Gaussian prior, i.e. an l2 description length). The soft WTA puts each cell's code into roughly one of M blocks, so sparsity moves from the synapses (l1) to the code (one active role per cell). This is Foldiak 1990's case for sparse, decorrelated codes feeding an associative layer.
replaces_lasso.guarantee_or_argument:
1) l1 is not load-bearing in this model. E1 (lambda 0 vs 0.01) gave 74/68, 84/87, 45/47 and 50/48 (single runs, noise +/-3-4). ISTA-30 gained at most +4. The old placement doc (section 3.1) already says least squares is exact for discrete content keys.
2) Pooled leave-one-out labelled cells per lane, computed here from the data files (6 lanes per group, EOS counted):
   - ARC-1 <=10: median 99, and 90% of lanes are below 256. At Mp = 256 the fit is underdetermined, so the min-norm selection and the early-stopping filter actually act.
   - ARC-2 eval demos: median 568, and 78% of lanes are at or above 256. The fit is overdetermined and selection is moot. The binding limit is the hypothesis family, which the wider code and the code targets attack.
3) Rejected alternatives:
   - Hard k-WTA on synapses (IHT): every exact fit becomes a fixed point, the guarantee needs RIP_3s, and in float64 checks it recovered the rule less often (0.50 vs 1.00 at n = 30).
   - Fit-based EM routing: nonconvex, needs a second router synapse at the query, and responsibilities computed with a lane's own leave-one-out Theta leak that lane's labels into the other lanes' fits at first order.
4) Cost: min-norm cannot extrapolate beyond the span of the demonstration codes, which l1 can do for sparse rules (old toy, explicit position operator: 95% vs 25/400). In this model, position comes from the frames and perception, not from Theta.

replaces_lasso.lasso_function: Explaining-away of correlated features (the theta G term: decorrelation, anti-Hebbian).
replaces_lasso.replacement: Kept as the anti-Hebbian half of the delta rule, -Theta G_psi (own read x pre). This is lateral inhibition among synapses (LCA: Rozell et al. 2008; LISTA's 'mutual inhibition'). It now acts on the conjunctive code, so its off-diagonal blocks G[m,m'] = sum pi_m pi_m' phi phi^T / n make heads explain each other away in proportion to the cells they share. The gate softmax adds competition among hypotheses: a soft WTA among the head units of a cell (Nessler et al. 2013; Maass 2000).
replaces_lasso.guarantee_or_argument:
Checked in float64:
- With hard gates, G_psi is block-diagonal and the joint fit equals M independent per-head regressions (1.4e-14).
- With soft gates, the cross-head blocks are nonzero (heads inhibit each other through -Theta G).
One term therefore gives both levels of competition: among synapses within a head (convex, LCA) and among heads for a cell. G_psi stays symmetric, so the convergence/energy argument for Landweber/LCA on a symmetric Gram is kept (Balavoine et al. 2012; Foldiak's symmetric-feedback condition). This corrects the handoff's framing: WTA here is competition among units/hypotheses, and the delta rule is competition among synapses; they are two axes, not alternatives.

replaces_lasso.lasso_function: Noise threshold: lambda ~ kappa/sqrt(n) (universal threshold) suppresses coefficients supported by few demo cells.
replaces_lasso.replacement: The spectral filter of finite recursion. After T = J x blocks steps from 0, the fit along an eigen-direction of G with demo energy s is multiplied by 1 - (1 - eta s)^T. Directions with s << lmax/T are suppressed: features few demo cells excite, and heads that own few cells. The effect is like ridge with rho ~ lmax/T (early stopping as regularisation; Landweber 1951, Engl-Hanke-Neubauer 1996, Yao-Rosasco-Caponnetto 2007, all from memory and to be verified). Where the rule synapse says little, the slow default classifier(h) answers. There is no hand-set kappa.
replaces_lasso.guarantee_or_argument:
- Checked: T steps equal the filter (4.8e-15), and |Theta_T| <= T eta |S|. This also bounds the new d-wide feedback W_fv rv.
- Data: the ARC-2 lambda sweep (0.0025 vs 0.005) made no difference; raising lambda only at evaluation was monotonically worse; learned lambda collapses without weight decay.
- Honest: the filter opens as recursion lengthens (16 segments x 16 blocks x J), and in that limit only the span restriction remains. That limit is the same as theorem 0's lambda -> 0+ (condition C).

replaces_lasso.lasso_function: Guarantee (theorem 0): S (rule in the family), L (sparse in the code), I (null-space property of the demo measurement) and C (convergence, lambda -> 0+) imply that the lasso minimiser is the true rule and the query answer is exact.
replaces_lasso.guarantee_or_argument:
- Off the span, the error is exactly -Theta*(I - P_D) psi*(o) (checked: 3.5e-14). So (I') is a certificate, |(I - P_D) psi*(o)|, that can be computed and logged per query cell at evaluation. The null-space property cannot be certified for a learned code.
- Fixed-point invariance: a recursion kernel on S and G with DC gains k_h, k_a > 0 (any shape, any odd part) converges to (k_h/k_a) times the same fit with the argmax unchanged (checked: 2.6e-10). The guarantee lives in the DC (Hebbian) part, and the odd part only shapes the path.
- Compared with theorem 0: weaker, because a sparse rule cannot be extrapolated beyond the span; stronger, because the condition can be checked.
- On ARC-2 lanes (n >= Mp) the certificate is almost always satisfied trivially, so exactness rests on S' alone, exactly where the failure is.
- Like theorem 0, it says nothing when S' fails. The existence and reachability of the joint fixed point are not proven.

design:expressivity-for-ARC-2.story:
Hebb's rule, as formalised, has no time. Fast weights and linear attention inherited it (Schlag et al. 2021), as did the delta rule of DeltaNet. Recurrent transformers (HRM, TRM, URM) made recursion depth a time axis but keep no memory across it. We put plasticity on that axis in the two places the task structure allows.

Within a pair, perception's fast weights follow a temporally asymmetric Hebbian rule with eligibility traces and a learned two-sided kernel over depth. Its DC part is the Hebbian term; its odd part vanishes at fixed points and records the trajectory (Xie & Seung 2000; Kempter et al. 1999, the latter to verify).

Between pairs, the only path from the demonstrations to the query is the rule synapse (proposition 4), and there the same form takes the shape TEM suggests. TEM's memory binds the code generated from structure (p-hat) to the code inferred with the observation (p) via M <- lambda M + eta (p - p-hat)(p + p-hat)^T (Whittington et al. 2020). We take the two phases literally: every demonstration runs through the same network twice. It runs free, exactly as the query must, and clamped, with its answer visible; these are the free and clamped phases of contrastive Hebbian learning and Equilibrium Propagation.

At each recursion step the rule synapse first predicts each demonstration cell's clamped state from its free code, then observes it. An asymmetric pairing window turns this predict-then-observe change of the postsynaptic state into the delta rule (Xie & Seung; Bengio et al. 2015). Its Hebbian half moves the synapse toward the observed association (LTP-like). Its anti-Hebbian half moves it away from the predicted association (LTD-like) and is lateral inhibition among synapses (LCA, Rozell et al. 2008). So explaining-away needs no extra mechanism and no threshold.

Competition is among hypotheses: rule heads compete for each cell by soft WTA. This makes the key a conjunctive code, role x structure, just as TEM's memory code is structure x sensation. The same anti-Hebbian term now makes both synapses and heads explain each other away.

The synapse has content rows (the observed colour) and transition rows (the observed code). Reading the transition rows, the query receives the state it would be in if it saw its answer. Injected into the next step, this turns the recursion into a procedure whose update rule is solved from the demonstrations. Because the demonstrations run free through the same steps, they supply the fit at every intermediate stage. Compare learned generator composition in our torus toy, and transitions learned by STDP in WTA circuits (Kappel et al. 2014).

At a fixed point the odd lobe vanishes and the synapse is the minimum-norm fit. The query is exact whenever its code lies in the span of the demonstration codes, which the model can check per cell. The asymmetric kernel therefore matters in perception and along the path, not in the converged rule; the theory makes this precise, so it does not have to be defended empirically.

Today's head is the special case with one head, colour rows only and one unit step. The nearest precedent is Backpropamine (learned neuromodulated Hebbian plasticity). We claim only the combination: a cross-pair delta-rule fast weight over recursion depth, with TEM's two-phase targets, under proposition 4.

design:expressivity-for-ARC-2.decisive_experiment:
The main test is Experiment 1. Experiments 2 and 3 are secondary binaries. All runs are single runs from scratch, and the predictions below are written before running.

EXPERIMENT 1 (decisive: is the demos->query channel the ARC-2 hypothesis-family failure?)
- Harness: arc.small on data/arc2_eval_small.npz (358 trainable demonstration pairs of 120 ARC-2 evaluation tasks, 172 test pairs).
- Config: docs/evidence/small/arc2eval_rope1d_lam005 (canvas 31, 8/4, 1D fixed RoPE, frames 8, batch 64, 20k steps) with the new head: M = 4, J = 4, power step, no lambda.
- The only switch:
  - arm A: transition rows on (clamped stream, Y = [y; phic], W_fv);
  - arm B: transition rows off (Y = y, no clamped stream).
- If arm A does not fit in FP32 traces at batch 64, both arms use trace_dtype bfloat16. Decide this before starting.
- Metrics:
  - train-batch exact (train.jsonl), mean over steps 10-15k and 15-20k;
  - test cell accuracy and changed-cell accuracy (scripts/analysis/cell_by_size.py) at 20k;
  - test exact /172.
- Lasso control in the same harness: train exact 0.065 (10-15k) and 0.145 (15-20k); test exact 0/172; test cell accuracy 0.745. For reference, ARC-1 <=10 reaches 0.461 and 0.542 in the same windows.
- Predictions:
  - P1 (removing the lasso costs nothing): arm B is within +/-0.04 of the lasso control in both windows.
  - P2 (the channel is binding): arm A reaches at least 0.20 in 10-15k and at least 0.35 in 15-20k, and arm A's test changed-cell accuracy is at least arm B's + 0.08.
  - P3: test exact is at most 3/172 in both arms. 358 pairs are too few for the slow decoder; this is a test of S, not of score.
- Decision:
  - If P2 holds, the paper may say the ARC-2 hypothesis-family failure is (at least partly) the narrow demos->query channel, and that TEM-style clamped targets widen it.
  - If P2 fails while P1 holds, the limit is in slow perception or data at canvas 31. Drop the expressivity claim and present the head only as the reformulation (provided Experiment 3 passes).

EXPERIMENT 2 (competition)
- Same harness. Arm C = arm A with M = 1 (no WTA; the code is phi, 64-dimensional).
- On ARC-2 the pooled labelled cells per lane (median 568) overdetermine a 64-dimensional map about 9 times.
- Prediction: if competition widens S, arm A beats arm C by at least +0.08 train exact in 15-20k. If |A - C| < 0.04, the WTA heads are only a reformulation and the paper must say so.

EXPERIMENT 3 (no regression on ARC-1 <=10)
- arc.small on arc1_ctx10_trans with the b8g4_rope1d config (50k steps), using arm A's head.
- Control: the existing from-scratch lasso run b8g4_rope1d (mean 101.4 exact /278 over 30-50k; train exact 0.734).
- Prediction: the mean over 30-50k is between 96 and 110. 90% of <=10 lanes have fewer than 256 pooled cells, so the Mp = 256 code is underdetermined and the early-stopping filter and min-norm selection are exercised.
  - Below 95 means the wider code overfits <=10 demonstrations, so p per head must shrink. Fix in advance: p = 16, Mp = 64.
  - Above 110 would mean the channel limits ARC-1 too.

PREREQUISITES AND COST
- CPU checks first: the reduction unit test (bit-equal to the lam = 0 head), and the float64 checks at /tmp/claude-0/-workspace-arc1-coupled/ae142cb7-3355-47e0-b126-2adf442a38bb/scratchpad/theory_wta/checks_wta.py, which already pass.
- Cost: arms A and C take about 2.2 h each, arm B about 1.1 h, Experiment 3 about 1.4 h. That is about 7 GPU-hours on one H100.
- GPU work ended on 10-28 by user decision, so this needs the user's go-ahead.
- The torus toy is not the right stage: its task family is closed under composition and needs no transition rows, as its own handoff notes.
risks: The core claim is untested. P2 can fail: the ARC-2 hypothesis-family failure may lie in slow perception or in data scarcity (358 pairs at canvas 31) rather than in the 13-dimensional channel. In that case the head is only a cleaner explanation, not an ARC-2 fix, and expected test exact stays at about 0-3/172 either way.

Compute and memory: the clamped stream doubles perception on demo lanes, which in training is every lane. That is about 2x step time and about 2x carry. The arc2eval lasso run already used 39.5 GB at batch 64, so arm A may need trace_dtype bfloat16 in both arms.

Training leakage gets wider. The second-order path y_A -> phic_A -> Theta_B -> r_B -> h_B -> psi_B -> Theta_A is now 13+p dimensions wide instead of 13. N is exact at evaluation, because test lanes are never clamped. Measure it with the holdout split (the 8/4 1D holdout run found held-out pairs at 28%, about the test rate). The fallback is a context/target split of the lanes in training.

Degenerate targets. phic may collapse onto phi (clamped perception ignores the answer) or onto a re-embedding of y. Then the transition rows add nothing and arm A equals arm B. Tying W_phi for key and target is a design choice fixed before running; untying it (a separate W_c) would be a different architecture.

No intermediate targets. The transition rows regress the clamped (final-answer) state at every step, so a procedure must be expressible as a fixed-point iteration of a map from the current state to the final state whose partial-progress states are linearly informative. There is no proof that this covers ARC-2's ordered procedures, e.g. writing along a path.

Min-norm loses l1's extrapolation for sparse rules beyond the span of the demonstration codes (old toy: 95% vs 25/400 for an explicit position operator). On ARC-2 lanes (n >= Mp) the span certificate is almost always satisfied trivially, so exactness rests on S' alone and the certificate is informative mainly at <=10.

WTA failure modes. Near-uniform gates give psi of about phi/M in every block, which is equivalent to one head; collapse onto a single head is also possible. Breaking the symmetry needs a random W_pi init. Log gate entropy and head usage. Straight-through hard gates may make training noisy.

Convergence. The step eta = 0.9/lhat overshoots if the power-iteration estimate is below lmax/2. The joint perception-rule map has no contraction proof. The d-wide feedback reopens the old instability risk (the multilinear fast side blew up in the old repo). The mitigation is that Theta is linear and |Theta_T| <= T eta |S|.

Novelty boundaries. The free/clamped phases come from contrastive Hebbian learning and Equilibrium Propagation (Movellan 1990, from memory; Scellier & Bengio 2017). Aggregating context pairs for a query resembles Neural Processes (Garnelo et al. 2018, from memory). Backpropamine is the precedent for learned plasticity. Claim only the combination.

Schedule. About 7 GPU-hours are needed before the 11-08 paper deadline, after GPU work was ended on 10-28. Without them the paper may present this only as a limitation and next step, and must not claim that it widens S.

Citations from memory still need verification: TEM-t (Whittington et al. 2022), Kempter et al. 1999, Movellan 1990, Garnelo et al. 2018, Jordan & Jacobs 1994 (EM for mixtures of experts, the rejected alternative), Landweber 1951, Engl-Hanke-Neubauer 1996, Yao-Rosasco-Caponnetto 2007, and the journal constant of Blumensath & Davies 2009. Web-checked by the grounding: Whittington 2020 update equation, Rozell 2008, Xie & Seung 1999/2000, Bengio et al. 2015/2017, Nessler 2013, Kappel 2014, Foldiak 1990, Balavoine 2012, Schlag 2021, DeltaNet, Miconi 2019.

design:biology-faithful.name: Plateau-gated three-factor rule synapse with a soft winner-take-all colour readout
design:biology-faithful.one_sentence: Each recursion block becomes one predict-then-observe cycle. First the colour units of every demonstration cell compete by lateral inhibition (a soft WTA, q = softmax(theta phi + sum_k Gamma_k kappa_k)). Then the observed colour arrives as a plateau-like teaching event, and a classical STDP window across that event writes (y~ - q) phi^T: the clamped-minus-free delta rule for a WTA readout, with y~ the label smoothed by the net-LTD lobe ratio. The tags of these changes decay over blocks and act again only while the lane's internal dopamine, the TD error of its demonstration consistency, is non-negative. Every temporal term vanishes at the fixed point, which is the maximum-entropy colour assignment that reproduces the demonstrations' Hebbian moments, and the small-signal limit of the update is exactly the current lambda = 0 lasso step.
design:biology-faithful.equations:
NOTATION (arc/model.py). Lanes l, m. Output-canvas cells o (O = C^2). VOCAB = 13. Valid colour units V = {2..12} (colours + EOS), K = |V| = 11. P_V = colour-centring on V (I - 11^T/K). p = cfg.phi. F = cfg.frames + 1. Blocks t.
Constant per segment: y_m(o) one-hot [13]; w_m(o) = m_m(o) * demo_m; partners N(l) = {m : group_m = group_l, m != l} (= others[l,m]); n_l = max(1, sum_{m in N(l)} sum_o w_m(o)); smoothed teacher yt_m(o) = rho y_m(o) + (1 - rho) 1_V / K, with rho = A+/A- = 0.9 fixed.
Carry per lane (new entries marked *): h, ek, ev, w (bands, unchanged); theta_l [13,p] (rows 0,1 stay 0); gam_l [F]; *E_l [13,p] and *Eg_l [F] (eligibility tags); *v_l (critic value); r_l [O,13]. Init: theta = gam = E = Eg = r = 0, v = log(1/K).

After block t (h_t from block_step, unchanged):
(1) Codes, unchanged: phi_m(o) = W_phi h_m(o) / (|W_phi h_m(o)| + 1e-6); kappa_m,k(o) = frame_colours(...)_k, with sum_k |kappa_m,k(o)|^2 <= 1.
(2) Retrieval half: lane l's synapse predicts partner m's cells.
  a_lm(o) = theta_l phi_m(o) + sum_k gam_l,k kappa_m,k(o)                 [13]
  q_lm(o) = softmax_{c in V} a_lm(o)_c   (soft WTA through lateral inhibition; q = 0 on tokens 0, 1)
(3) Encoding half: the observed colour clamps the units (plateau-like event). STDP lobes across the event, read only at the plateau:
  raw change = A+ y phi^T (pre before the clamped post: LTP-like, toward the association teacher x pre)
             - A- q phi^T (free WTA post before pre: LTD-like, away from the association prediction x pre).
  Removing the colour-common part, which the WTA cannot see (heterosynaptic balance), gives A- (yt - q) phi^T. A- is absorbed into eta.
  D_lm(o) = yt_m(o) - q_lm(o)    (post change at the event; zero where the prediction already matches)
  H_l     = (1/n_l) sum_{m in N(l)} sum_o w_m(o) D_lm(o) phi_m(o)^T                      [13 x p]
  Hg_l,k  = (1/n_l) sum_{m in N(l)} sum_o w_m(o) < D_lm(o), kappa_m,k(o) >               [F]
(4) Demonstration consistency and internal dopamine (from the theta pass, demonstrations only):
  C_l = (1/n_l) sum_m sum_o w_m(o) < yt_m(o), log q_lm(o) >
  s_l = 1[ no labelled partner-demo cell has argmax q_lm(o) != argmax y_m(o) ]
  delta_l = C_l - v_l ;   v_l <- C_l + b (1 - s_l) ;   g_l = 1[delta_l >= 0]   (stop-gradient)
(5) Three-factor update (eligibility x dopamine), Gauss-Seidel as in the current step(): theta first, then gam with q recomputed from the new theta.
  E_l  <- H_l + g_l * kappa * E_l ;               theta_l <- theta_l + eta * E_l
  Eg_l <- Hg_l(new theta) + g_l * kappa * Eg_l ;  gam_l   <- gam_l + eta * Eg_l
  eta = 2 = 1/L per variable: diag q - q q^T <= (1/2) P_V (Boehning bound), so L_theta <= (1/2) lambda_max(G) <= (1/2) tr G <= 1/2, and L_gam <= (1/2) sum_k |kappa_k|^2 <= 1/2. Fixed kappa = 0.5; b = 0 in the decisive ARC run.
  Equivalent canonical three-factor form: d theta = eta (H_t + M_t E_{t-1}), with M_t = g_t kappa.
(6) Read, same interface as now: r_l(o) = theta_l phi_l(o) + sum_k gam_l,k kappa_l,k(o) on the lane's own cells, with the new theta and gam (units 0, 1 are 0). The next block gets fb = W_fb r; logits = classifier(h) + tau r (direct), bias + tau r (r-only), or the out_ffn path.

FIXED POINT (phi, kappa frozen): E = Eg = 0 and sum w (yt - q)[phi; kappa]^T = 0. This is the stationarity condition of the convex J_l = (1/n_l) sum w [ logsumexp_V a - < yt, a > ]. Dually it is max sum_o w H(q(o)) subject to sum w q phi^T = sum w yt phi^T and sum w <q, kappa_k> = sum w <yt, kappa_k>. The fixed point exists because yt is interior (rho < 1). It is unique in the reachable subspace (theta rows in span of the demo phi, colour-centred, because theta_0 = 0).
SMALL-SIGNAL LIMIT: H_l = (1/K) P_V (rho K S - theta G) + O(|a|^2), with G and S from the current statistics(). This is the lambda = 0 lasso step.
EXACTNESS: if s_l = 1 and (phi(o*), kappa(o*)) = sum_i alpha_i (phi(o_i), kappa(o_i)) with alpha_i >= 0 and y(o_i) = c* for all i, then argmax_V r(o*) = c*.

replaces_lasso.lasso_function: Selection principle (min l1 = shortest description among the theta consistent with the demonstrations)
replaces_lasso.replacement: Maximum entropy under the WTA. The fixed point is the colour-belief assignment of largest entropy over the other demonstrations' labelled cells that reproduces their Hebbian moments, sum w yt phi^T and sum w <yt, kappa_k>. Equivalently it is the minimiser of the rho-smoothed demonstration cross-entropy in the reachable subspace. As rho -> 1 it should approach the maximum-margin rule (from memory, to verify).
replaces_lasso.guarantee_or_argument: H = 0 is exactly the moment-matching condition. A Gibbs (softmax) form plus moment matching is the maximum-entropy dual (Jaynes 1957; Berger, Della Pietra & Della Pietra 1996; both from memory). The fixed point exists because yt is interior (rho < 1, Slater). It is unique because logsumexp is strictly convex on the colour-centred span, and theta_0 = 0 keeps theta in that span. Checked in float64: the unbalanced-lobe dynamics reach the smoothed-CE fixed point within 2.2e-14, and the moment residual of the converged reference is 4e-16 (scratchpad/wta/checks.py, checks2.py). Biological reading: the least committed belief consistent with the co-activity statistics. Proposition 4 is restated around this principle: the head is still the only cross-lane path, so the principle is fixed by structure. Caveat: when p >= the number of demo cells, moment matching becomes interpolation and the selection reduces to minimum-norm interpolation in logit space, with no sparsity (tested by E-B).

replaces_lasso.lasso_function: Explaining-away (the theta G term: anti-Hebbian lateral inhibition / decorrelation between synapses)
replaces_lasso.replacement: Shared prediction error through the WTA's free phase. The LTD-like lobe pairs the competition's own response q with pre (sum w q phi^T). A feature redundant with one that already makes the right colour win gets no further credit (Rescorla-Wagner / Kamin blocking). The effective inhibition between synapses (c,j) and (c',k) is sum_o w (diag q - q q^T)_cc' phi_j phi_k: the Gram G weighted by how undecided the competition is at each cell.
replaces_lasso.guarantee_or_argument: At the fixed point sum (yt - q) phi^T = 0, so the residual is orthogonal to every feature (GLM normal equations). The small-signal limit is H = (1/K) P_V (rho K S - theta G) + O(|a|^2). Checked: relative error 2.2e-3, 1.8e-5 and 2.2e-7 at drive scales 0.1, 0.01 and 0.001 (scratchpad/wta/checks4.py). So the lasso's theta G is the undecided-state limit of the WTA's anti-Hebbian term, and cells the competition has already decided stop mediating inhibition. The interaction is the Hessian of a convex function, so it stays symmetric and the settling argument for symmetric lateral interactions still applies.

replaces_lasso.lasso_function: Noise threshold (soft threshold lambda ~ kappa/sqrt(n): exact zeros, constant LTD with a floor)
replaces_lasso.replacement: Net-LTD lobe ratio rho = A+/A- < 1. After the colour-common change is removed, this acts as label smoothing, which gives a finite fixed point with bounded synapses. The synapse stops strengthening once the competition is won with confidence about rho + (1 - rho)/K: the aggregate logit margin is about log(1 + rho K/(1 - rho)) = 4.6 at rho = 0.9, K = 11. The event also has its own natural size: there is no plateau-driven change where the prediction already matches. theta_0 = 0 with a finite number of blocks acts as early stopping. There are no exact zeros.
replaces_lasso.guarantee_or_argument: Song, Miller & Abbott 2000: stable competitive STDP needs a negative window integral. Here that condition makes the objective coercive, so theta stays bounded. Checked: without removing the colour-common part, that part drifts (norm 5.25 after 2,000 steps); with it removed, the per-cell margin is at most 5.2 (the 4.6 ceiling is on the moments, not on each cell). Repo evidence that the zeros are not load-bearing for the current content map: lambda = 0 and 0.01 give the same exact counts in all four E1 settings, and a more exact solver adds at most +4.5 (r-only 60.3 -> 64.8 at 30k-50k). If exact zeros are ever needed (explicit position operators), they come back in max-ent form: l1-regularised max-ent is moment matching within a box of half-width lambda, with lambda ~ sigma/sqrt(n) the sampling error of the Hebbian moment (Dudik, Phillips & Schapire 2007, from memory). The kappa/sqrt(n) prior is then derived rather than assumed.

replaces_lasso.lasso_function: Guarantee (theorem 0: S, L, I = null-space property, C => exact query answer)
replaces_lasso.replacement: Categorical exactness proposition plus convergence C'. Let perception converge to (phi*, kappa*) and the head to its fixed point. If (i) the head explains every other demonstration cell (s = 1, computed from the demonstrations alone) and (ii) the query cell's joint code (phi*(o*), kappa*(o*)) lies in the cone generated by the demonstration cells whose answer is c*, then argmax r(o*) = c*. No sparsity and no null-space property are needed.
replaces_lasso.guarantee_or_argument: Proof: the colour margins of a linear read are linear in the joint code, so (a_c* - a_c)(o*) = sum_i alpha_i (a_c* - a_c)(o_i) > 0 (numerically 1.0 on random cases). The argument holds for any linear read whose argmax is right on the demonstrations, so the cone tier also holds for the lasso. C': the update is gradient descent on a convex objective with curvature <= 1/2 (Boehning 1992, from memory), with step 1/L per variable. Every fixed point of the (theta, E) system has E = 0 and hence H = 0, so the trace and the dopamine gate change only the path. Checked: kappa = 0.5 and 0.8 approach the same reference (relative difference 3.5e-2 and 2.4e-3), faster than kappa = 0. Conditions (i) and C' are observable at run time, which theorem 0's I was not. This is an interpolation guarantee only: theorem 0's extrapolation-by-sparsity claim is dropped. That claim was never certifiable, and its premise C was not met by the deployed one-step iterate. Condition N (exact at evaluation, first order in training) and proposition 4 hold structurally, as now.

design:biology-faithful.story:
Hebb's postulate was causal ('takes part in firing it'). The formal rule dw ~ pre x post dropped time, and the fast-weight -> linear-attention -> delta-rule lineage inherited that timeless form (Schlag et al. 2021; DeltaNet). Recurrent reasoners (HRM, TRM, URM) created a time axis, recursion depth, but keep no memory across it. Our model places two Hebbian outer-product memories on that axis and lets the timing of plasticity do work in both.

Within a pair (perception), each head's bands memory pairs a token with itself across blocks through a learned two-sided kernel. Its DC part is the Hebbian term; its odd part vanishes at fixed points and records the trajectory (Xie & Seung 1999; the Kempter decomposition, from memory).

Between pairs (the rule synapse, the only path from the demonstrations to the query), each block is one predict-then-observe cycle. These are the two phases the hippocampal theta rhythm has been proposed to separate: retrieval, then encoding (Hasselmo, Bodelon & Wyble 2002, from memory).
- Retrieval half: the colour units of every demonstration output cell compete by lateral inhibition and settle into a soft winner-take-all response, q = softmax(theta phi + sum_k Gamma_k kappa_k). Softmax is the rate-level form of a stochastic WTA circuit (Nessler et al. 2013). This is the task rule's prediction for that cell.
- Encoding half: the observed colour arrives as a plateau-like instructive event and clamps the units. Biological analogues are BTSP (Bittner et al. 2017) and the EC3 teaching input that directs CA1 learning (Grienberger & Magee 2022); both are from memory.
- An STDP window that straddles the event, read out only around the plateau as in BTSP, has two lobes: LTP-like for pre before the clamped post, LTD-like for the free post before the pre. It writes A+ y phi^T - A- q phi^T. The WTA cannot see colour-common changes, and once they are balanced out the result is (y~ - q) phi^T, with y~ the label smoothed by the lobe ratio. The ratio is net LTD, the condition Song, Miller & Abbott (2000) found necessary for stable competitive STDP.

This one expression is three standard things at once:
- the clamped-minus-free difference of Boltzmann-machine learning (Ackley, Hinton & Sejnowski 1985, from memory);
- the differential-Hebbian reading of STDP, in which pre times the change of post is a gradient step (Xie & Seung 1999; Bengio et al. 2017; Scellier & Bengio 2017);
- the hetero-associative form of TEM's own memory update, M <- lambda M + eta (p - p^)(p + p^)^T. There the prediction p^ comes from the structure code and p from the observation (Whittington et al. 2020).

The constant teacher has become an event whose size is the prediction error, so the y-constant problem disappears. The post signal that drives plasticity changes along recursion and falls to zero exactly when the demonstrations are explained.

The changes leave tags (an eligibility trace) that decay over blocks. The tags act again only while the lane's internal dopamine, the temporal-difference error of its demonstration consistency, is non-negative; a dip erases them. This is a three-factor rule (Fremaux & Gerstner 2016; dopamine acting retroactively on STDP: Brzosko, Schultz & Paulsen 2015, from memory), and the same signal drives the search in the torus toy. The critic expects progress only while the demonstrations are unexplained, so the signal vanishes at a solution: the literature's fix for the toy's consolidation failure (Fremaux, Sprekeler & Gerstner 2010).

At the fixed point every temporal term vanishes: the odd lobe, the trace and the dopamine. What remains is moment matching. Among all colour beliefs over the demonstration cells that reproduce the observed colour-feature co-activities, the synapse settles on the maximum-entropy one. The guarantee is therefore categorical: whenever the rule explains every other demonstration cell (observable) and the query cell's code lies in the cone of demonstration cells with the same answer, the query is exact.

TEM's factorisation applies directly:
- phi and the frames' position-keyed softmax reads (the TEM-t retrieval) are the structure code;
- the colour units are the sensory prediction, which TEM also makes as a softmax;
- theta and Gamma are the per-task binding written from the demonstrations;
- answering the query is TEM's generative path.
Two competitions sit at the two ends of one fast synapse: the frames' softmax over input cells chooses where to read, and the colour units' softmax chooses what to answer.

Finally, the current head is this circuit's small-signal limit. Linearising the competition at the undecided state gives (1/K) P_V (rho K S - theta G), the lambda = 0 lasso step. So the published code changes by one nonlinearity and one timing convention, and the measured irrelevance of lambda (E1) fits this account. No new terms are needed: soft WTA, lateral inhibition, plateau potential, STDP lobes, eligibility trace, three-factor rule, TD error, maximum entropy and label smoothing are all standard.

Where it plugs in: arc/model.py, rule head only. Perception, bands, frames, W_phi, W_fb, tau, out_ffn, logits and evaluate.py/submission() are unchanged, because r keeps its [L,O,13] meaning.
- ModelConfig: rule: str = 'lasso' | 'wta', plus wta_rho = 0.9, wta_kappa = 0.5, wta_b = 0.0, wta_eta = 2.0. Defaults keep the current head bit-identical.
- New method wta_head(h, x_in, y, m, demo, partner, theta, gam, E, Eg, v, amp, ftab), dispatched from rule_head when cfg.rule == 'wta'. It reuses features() and frame_colours(). statistics(), step(), soft() and lam_raw stay for the lasso arm and are unused by 'wta'.
- Pair drives: A = einsum('lcp,ljop->ljoc', theta, phi[partner]) + einsum('lf,ljfoc->ljoc', gam, kap[partner]), shape [L,M-1,O,13]. partner is a static [L, M-1] index of the other lanes of each group (padded to a dummy slot with w = 0). arc/small.py already packs groups contiguously, at most D+1 = 6 lanes, so M-1 = 5; the batcher builds partner on the host as one more batch tensor.
- Masking: units 0 and 1 get a -1e4 bias (not -inf), so yt*log q stays finite. q = softmax(A); D = w_pair*(yt - q).
- Contractions: H = einsum('ljoc,ljop->lcp', D, phi[partner]) / n; Hg = einsum('ljoc,ljfoc->lf', D, kap[partner]) / n; C and s are reductions over the same tensor. The Gamma pass recomputes A with the new theta (a second pass, Gauss-Seidel as now).
- Proposition 4: the partner gather is the only cross-lane operation, replacing others @ P, so it stays exact. The diagonal (own lane) is never in partner, so leave-one-out is exact at first order, as now.
- Carry: initial_carry adds E [L,13,p] = 0, Eg [L,F] = 0, v [L] = log(1/K). layer() threads them. segment() detaches them with theta/r/gam at i == first_grad and on return.
- Compile / CUDA graphs: static shapes; softmax, einsum, argmax, torch.where for the gate, no .item(), no data-dependent shapes. It stays inside the compiled layer like the current head (FP32, autocast off). No new host syncs.
- Differentiability: the soft WTA is smooth, so the gradients to W_phi, W_fq/W_fk/frame_omega, W_fb and tau are smoother than the soft threshold's almost-everywhere derivative. The dopamine gate is detached, so no straight-through is needed. The hypergradient is still truncated at grad_blocks unrolled steps, as now (the truncated bilevel backprop of docs/blocks_and_backprop.md).
- Cost: <=10 harness (L = 64, M-1 = 5, O = 121): pair tensors of about 0.5M floats per pass, negligible. Full ARC (O = 900, larger groups): tens of MB per saved tensor per block. With grad_blocks = 10 this is a few GB, so activation checkpointing of the head may be needed. The head loses the sufficient-statistics property: each step is one pass over the demonstration cells, instead of iterating on [p,p] matrices.
