design:biology-faithful.decisive_experiment:
All predictions below are written before any run.

E-A (<=10 harness, from scratch, binary: lasso head vs this head; needs one GPU and the user's go-ahead, since GPU work on 4xH100 ended 10-28). One run with rule='wta' (rho 0.9, kappa 0.5, b 0, eta 2), 50k steps. Everything else is identical to docs/evidence/small/e1_b8g4_ronly_lam0.01_100k: 8/4, learned 2D RoPE, frames 8, direct_head False (r-only), batch 64, lr 3e-4.
- r-only is chosen because the answer is then the head's own read, so the selection principle decides it; in the direct-head configuration perception can mask the head.
- Existing controls (30k-50k interval mean, 21 evals): lasso one-step 60.3/278 (range 58-63); ISTA-30 (b8g4_ronly_ista30_lam0.01) 64.8 (61-69).
- P1: interval mean >= 58. The replacement claim is rejected if it is <= 56. Expected 60-66: the CPU synthetic with the same tr-G step put the heads within 1-2 points of cell accuracy at 8 blocks (lasso 0.766, WTA+trace 0.749).
- P2: synapses stay bounded. The maximum demonstration-cell logit margin of the head stays < 10 throughout, with no NaN.
- P3: a mean > 67 (above ISTA-30) would mean the categorical fixed point helps beyond solver precision. I do not expect this.
- Only if P1 holds: the direct-head 8/4 1D fixed-RoPE run against docs/evidence/small/b8g4_rope1d (30k-50k mean 101.3, range 96-105). Prediction >= 98.

E-B (torus toy, CPU minutes, binary: l1 vs max-ent selection where the old theory says l1 is needed). Use the exact frame code as the structure code. For output cell o, phi(o) = concat over all 128 t of onehot5(colour of apply_t(input, t) at o) / sqrt(128), with read a = theta phi, theta in R^{5 x 640}. The true rule is one nonzero per colour row. Each instance has 48 demonstration cells. Both heads are solved to convergence on the same features over all 3,072 instances:
- lasso: one-hot regression, lambda 1e-4, FISTA to KKT residual 1e-10;
- this head: smoothed CE, rho 0.9, to moment residual 1e-10.
Metric: query exact (all 16 cells right).
- Predictions: lasso >= 0.85; WTA head <= 0.30. Reason: 640 features >= 48 cells, so moment matching becomes interpolation and max-ent becomes minimum-norm interpolation in logit space, the regime where the old toy without a threshold got 25/400.
- Decision: if WTA >= lasso - 0.05, max-ent selection suffices even for explicit position operators and the replacement is complete. If WTA <= lasso - 0.30, the replacement holds only for content maps (the deployed theta), and any future positional theta must restore l1 in max-ent form (moment tolerance lambda ~ sigma/sqrt(n)). That restored form then becomes the follow-up arm.

E-C (torus search, CPU, check of the shared dopamine definition). Existing dopamine condition (fixed b) vs a critic that expects progress only while unsolved: v = r_{n-1} + b * 1[r_{n-1} < 1]. Trajectories are identical until the first success by construction (same seed).
- Prediction: relapse-free stay after success rises from 0.045 to >= 0.90. Steps and success are unchanged.
risks: Elegance verdict, stated plainly: the explanation becomes very clean. There is one nonlinearity (lateral inhibition among colour units) and one timing convention (predict, then observe), every term has a textbook plasticity name, the fixed point is maximum entropy, the current head is its small-signal limit, and TEM's update is the same form. The mechanism does not become more powerful. The math is softmax regression plus heavy-ball momentum with restart, and reviewers may call the biology a renaming. The paper must present it as a reading of standard mathematics, with precise citations, not as evidence.

Sparsity and the null-space-property guarantee are dropped. For explicit position operators (the extrapolation tier) max-ent likely reduces to minimum-norm interpolation, the regime where the old toy failed (25/400 without a threshold). E-B is designed to show this. If it does, l1 must come back as a max-ent moment tolerance for any future positional theta.

Slower at a finite number of blocks. Near the undecided state the CE curvature is about 1/K of the least-squares curvature, so with the worst-case step the head moves more slowly early on. Synthetic, 8 blocks, tr-G step: query cell accuracy 0.749 (WTA+trace) vs 0.766 (lasso); n=300 setting 0.681 vs 0.691. With a per-lane step 1/lambda_max(G), both heads improve and the WTA head is ahead at 30 blocks (0.926 vs 0.884; 0.832 vs 0.767). But that step is a separate lever, ISTA-30 showed at most +4.5, and using it in only one arm would confound the comparison.

The guarantee is interpolation-only. The cone proposition holds for any linear read with correct demonstration argmax, including the lasso, so the new head's guarantee is not stronger. It is simpler and checkable at run time. Consistency on the demonstrations (s = 1) is observed, not implied: at rho < 1 the smoothed fixed point can misclassify a demonstration cell when margins are tight. The max-margin limit as rho -> 1 is from memory or conjecture.

The dopamine has a modest job. In the convex head it only gates momentum (restart) and is guarantee-neutral at the fixed point. Its contribution may not show in ARC exact counts (in the torus toy the trace added little). Its real role, search in the nonconvex joint perception-rule system, is not exercised by this head.

Cost and memory: per-pair drives [L, M-1, O, 13] replace the [p,p] sufficient statistics. It is cheap at <=10, but at full ARC (O = 900, large groups) it needs checkpointing. The old 'many cheap prox iterations on small matrices' path to a true condition C is lost.

The biological mapping is idealised. BTSP is mostly potentiating (Bittner 2017) and is bidirectional only in a weight-dependent way (Milstein 2021). The error-driven reading of plateaus (Grienberger & Magee 2022), the theta-phase separation of encoding and retrieval (Hasselmo 2002), the restriction of the window to pairings that straddle the plateau, the heterosynaptic removal of colour-common change, and dopamine erasing tags (Brzosko 2015) are interpretations or simplifications. All are cited from memory and need checking against the sources.
Fixed rho = 0.9 caps the aggregate read margin at about 4.6 logits. In r-only mode the learned tau must supply the rest of the confidence, which could slow training.

Unchanged weaknesses: the joint perception-head fixed point is unproven; condition N is exact only at evaluation, and a second-order leakage path still exists in training; the hypothesis family is still argmax of a linear read of a learned per-cell code plus frames. The classification constraint is slightly looser than one-hot regression, but the ARC-2 condition-S failure (procedural rules, 0/172) is untouched and must stay a stated limitation.
The CPU synthetic is not ARC: unit Gaussian-cluster features and 20 tasks per setting. It only supports the finite-T comparison; it is not evidence about the learned phi.

fatal_flaws: Experiment 1 cannot attribute a P2 win to the demos->query channel. Arm A changes four things at once relative to arm B. (a) It adds a stream that perceives the answer grids, and through S -> Theta -> rv -> W_fv that stream trains the shared slow weights on answers, which is auxiliary representation learning. (b) It roughly doubles perception compute. (c) It widens the training-time second-order leak from 13 to 13+p dimensions. (d) It adds a d-wide feedback path, W_fv. The decision metric is train-batch exact on the 358 pairs the model trains on, where every lane is both a demonstration and a query. That metric mixes memorisation, slow capacity and leakage with channel expressivity. A P2 pass therefore does not show that 'the narrow channel is the S failure'. A P2 fail is also ambiguous, because phic can collapse.

Neither the min-norm selection principle nor the span certificate holds for the iteration as deployed. Theta is warm-started across blocks (and segments) while psi drifts every block. Under (I - eta G_t), components of Theta in the null space of the current Gram have factor 1, so they never decay. The limit is therefore not the min-norm fit of the final code, and query reads pick up stale components. Float64 toy (scratchpad/review_wta/drift.py: n=30, p=64, 8 drifting blocks x 4 steps): |Theta (I - P_final)| = 12.4, against 0 for min-norm. The out-of-span read is 1.19 and the in-span error is 0.335, against 0.072 for a fresh Landweber run of the same length. In the lasso head the soft threshold (constant LTD) was the only thing that forgot stale coefficients; removing it removes all decay. This is a lasso function the proposal does not list, and losing it invalidates replacement #1 and theorem 0' as stated.

The 'transition rows' are not transitions, so the ARC-2 expressivity claim has no mechanism. phic_t is the clamped stream's code at the same depth t. That stream sees the full answer from block 1, so its depth trajectory is a refinement of a known answer, not intermediate states of a procedure. The phrase 'the recursion runs a procedure whose update rule is solved from the demonstrations' is therefore unsupported. What is actually added is a per-cell linear predictor of a 64-d answer-aware code: more bandwidth (77·Mp instead of 13·Mp transferred numbers), but every row is still linear in psi(o). Kappel et al. 2014, cited as precedent, learns lagged state transitions, and nothing here is lagged.

The STDP reading (section 8 and the one-sentence summary) is not implemented, and taken literally it cancels. Each block computes (Y - rhat) psi^T algebraically, with no window. A persistent pairing window over the recursion's alternating predict/observe train (rhat, Y, rhat, Y, ...) with constant pre gives only a boundary term. In drift.py, one predict->observe pair gives 0.485, but eight alternating pairs give 0.729 instead of 3.88. The window must be reset or gated at every observation, which is an extra third factor. Since the paper's main thesis is the temporally asymmetric kernel, calling the rule synapse 'the predict->observe form of an asymmetric pairing window' would read to a judge as decoration. The rule synapse here has no temporal kernel; its only history is warm-start accumulation with decay (I - eta G_t).
errors_in_math_or_citations: The step-size claim '1/lmax is about 55x the tr G bound at p=64, M=4' comes from isotropic random codes (checks_wta.py #6). I measured trained codes on runs/small/e1_b8g4_direct_lam0.0/last.pt (CPU, eval batch, scratchpad/review_wta/gram_spectrum.py). There lmax(G) has median 0.31-0.61 with tr G = 1 across the 8 blocks, so 1/lmax is only 1.6-3.1x the current step 1, and the effective rank tr/lmax is about 1.6-3.1. The '55x' should be removed or re-measured at canvas 31.

The span certificate |(I - P_D) psi*| is vacuous on trained codes. On the same checkpoint (p=64, about 100 pooled cells), the leave-one-out demo codes have full numerical rank, 64 of 64 at tolerance 1e-6·lmax. The query residual is 0.000 on every lane, yet only 5 eigenvalues exceed lmax/32. Whether the exact-span condition holds depends on the tolerance chosen. The certificate that means something is the finite-T one. For Theta_0 = 0 and fixed G with S = Theta* G, Theta_T = Theta*(I - (I - eta G)^T) exactly (checked: 6.7e-15), so the query error is -Theta*(I - eta G)^T psi*. Measured median |(I - eta G)^T phi_q| is 0.28 for today's step (eta=1, T=8) and 0.20 for the proposal's (eta=0.9/lmax, T=32) (scratchpad/review_wta/cert.py).

Internal inconsistency between replacements #3 and #4. Noise suppression relies on finite T (the early-stopping filter), while theorem 0' relies on convergence (C', T -> infinity). Both cannot hold at once. The finite-T identity above resolves this, because the filter and the guarantee become a single formula.

Theorem 0' for the code rows is missing a condition. Exactness of the code read rv does not imply an exact answer. A decodability condition is needed: the slow decoder must map the injected clamped-code prediction to the answer.

'The query receives exactly the code it would have computed with its answer visible' is wrong as stated. The clamped stream runs with fb = None while the free stream has feedback, so phic belongs to a different dynamical system (perception without feedback). It is not the query's own counterfactual, and it is not EqProp's nudged phase (same energy plus beta·cost).

The CHL/EqProp analogy is loose. CHL updates by Hebb(clamped) - Hebb(free) of the same pre/post. The proposal's update is (Y_clamped - rhat) psi_free^T, a cross-phase product (clamped post x free pre), which is the plain Widrow-Hoff/delta rule. Likewise TEM's update (p - p_hat)(p + p_hat)^T has pre factor (p + p_hat), not the free code, so 'S - Theta G is its hetero-associative version' matches only in the error factor.

Foldiak 1990 is cited in support of the soft-WTA code ('sparsity moves to the code'). Foldiak argues against WTA (one unit per combination) and for decorrelated distributed codes, which is the opposite of the use here.

Nessler et al. 2013 and Maass 2000 are cited for 'competition among hypotheses'. The gates are a softmax of slow-learned perception logits and do not depend on the fit, so this is input-dependent mixture-of-experts gating (Jacobs, Jordan, Nowlan & Hinton 1991, from memory) and equals a wider feature map. It is not Nessler-style posterior competition among causes. The proposal's own grounding 3 says this.

'Sparsity moves from the synapses to the code' mixes up two things. Code sparsity changes the hypothesis family (the representation), not the rule that selects among the Theta consistent with the demos. That rule is min-l2 in psi coordinates, whose metric the slow weights choose.

'On ARC-2 lanes (n >= Mp) the fit is overdetermined and selection is moot' is a cell-count argument, not a rank argument. ARC-2 eval tasks have a median of 3 trainable pairs (34 tasks have 2), so a lane's leave-one-out set is often 1-2 other grids, and trained codes have effective rank about 2-3. The fit stays ill-conditioned. The numbers themselves reproduce: median 570 pooled cells, 78% >= 256; ARC-1 <=10 median 100, 90% < 256. The '6 lanes per group' description is inaccurate: groups have min(trainable pairs, D+1) lanes.

Missing closest ML precedents (all from memory; verify): von Oswald et al. 2023 ICML, 'Transformers learn in-context by gradient descent' (linear self-attention = one GD step on in-context least squares, i.e. exactly this delta-rule rule head); von Oswald et al. 2023, 'Uncovering mesa-optimization algorithms in Transformers' (a mesa-layer that solves regularised least squares over the context); Akyurek et al. 2023 ICLR, 'What learning algorithm is in-context learning?'. An ARC Prize judge will expect these ahead of Neural Processes.

Bengio et al. '2015' (arXiv:1509.05936, 'STDP as presynaptic activity times rate of change of postsynaptic activity') and the 2017 Neural Computation paper ('STDP-compatible approximation of backpropagation in an energy-based model') are different papers; cite each under its own title.

Minor: the FLOP estimate O(L O (Mp)^2) gives about 1.0 GFLOP at <=10 and about 8 GFLOP at canvas 31 when multiply-adds are counted, against the stated 0.5 and 4. The arc2eval lasso run peaked at 39.5 GB, so doubling the lanes in perception plus the backward pass through the clamped stream is very likely to exceed 80 GB at FP32 traces.
strongest_points: The reduction is exact and cheap to verify. With M=1, code rows off, J=1 and eta=1 the head is today's lam=0 head (soft(x,0)=x). E1 (74/68, 84/87, 45/47, 50/48) and the ARC-2 lambda sweep (lasso control 0.065/0.145 against 0.070/0.161 at lambda 0.0025, both verified from train.jsonl.gz) show l1 is not load-bearing, so dropping lambda is empirically free, and the bit-equality test anchors the change.

The free/clamped twin is a faithful instantiation of TEM's p_hat/p split (structure-only code vs observation-informed code). It gives thesis 2 a concrete mechanism and widens the demos->query channel from 13·Mp to (13+p)·Mp transferred numbers without new cross-lane operations.
Proposition 4 really is kept in code: clamped twins are per lane, the only cross-lane operation is still others@P, test lanes have w = m*demo = 0 and xc = x, so condition N stays exact at evaluation.

The float64 checks pass when rerun: Landweber -> min-norm (3.8e-11), the span-error identity (3.5e-14), hard gates giving a block-diagonal G and per-head fits (1.4e-14), DC-gain invariance with argmax unchanged (2.6e-10), and the spectral filter (4.8e-15). Keeping the anti-Hebbian -Theta G term as explaining-away is correct.

Experiment 1 is a binary, from-scratch, pre-registered intervention. Its thresholds (+0.135 and +0.205 over the control) sit far above the observed run-to-run spread (about 0.016), and P3 honestly predicts test exact <= 3/172.

It is engineering-compatible. Shapes are static, there is no host sync, the power-iteration port already exists (.claude/worktrees/ista/arc/model.py lipschitz()), and concatenating free and clamped lanes in block_step is exact because lanes never mix.
The risk list is honest about the main failure modes: wider training leakage, target collapse, no intermediate targets, compute, and loss of l1 extrapolation for position operators.
fixes: Make the finite-T identity the theory hinge. For Theta_0 = 0 and fixed G, Theta_T = Theta*(I - (I - eta G)^T), so the query error is exactly -Theta*(I - eta G)^T psi*(o). Log |(I - eta G)^T psi*(o)| per query cell. This one formula is both the noise filter (function 3) and the guarantee (function 4), it removes the C'-vs-early-stopping conflict, and it is informative on trained codes (median 0.20-0.28), unlike the exact-span certificate (0.000 everywhere).

Fix the warm-start drift explicitly, and pre-register the choice. Option (a): a leak, Theta <- (1 - eta rho) Theta - eta(Theta G_t - S_t), i.e. ridge, which forgets stale null-space components. This is the honest one-sided exponential trace of the rule synapse and the delta-rule analogue of the bands' (1 - eta) decay. Option (b): restart Theta at 0 every block and run J steps, so the closed form holds per block. Either restores the min-norm/certificate claim.

Rename the 'transition rows' to clamped-code rows and drop the procedure and Kappel claims. Alternatively, make them real transitions by regressing a lagged target (phic_{t+1} from psi_t), the only version in which a temporally asymmetric (pre-leading) pairing has a job in the rule synapse. Choose one before running.

De-confound Experiment 1. One option is a matched-compute control arm whose clamped twins see a different group's answers (permute targets across groups): same compute and same answer-perception gradients, but no task information in the code rows. Then require A > A_perm as well as A > B. Another option is to stop-gradient the clamped stream in arm A (targets as data, as in CHL), which removes the auxiliary-learning confound, halves backward memory and removes the incentive for targets to collapse. In addition, in every arm mark one lane per training group demo=False (a context/target split, a training protocol rather than an eval-time ablation) and use that lane's exact as the decision metric, so the second-order leak cannot inflate it.

Make P1 test what it names. Either compare arm B to a control that differs only in lambda (same M, J and step), or rename P1 'Landweber with WTA vs one ISTA step'. Fix the trace dtype for all arms in advance, and rerun the control at bf16 if bf16 is needed.

For elegance, drop the M-head gate from the main design unless Experiment 2 runs first. By the proposal's own grounding it equals a wider phi, so describe it as mixture-of-experts gating (Jacobs et al. 1991) if it is kept, not as Nessler/Maass competition. The clean story is then: today's head with lambda removed, plus a clamped twin whose code is a second target.

Restate the temporal story honestly. The rule synapse is a DeltaNet-style delta rule over recursion with data-dependent decay (I - eta G_t), plus the leak from the second fix. The pairing-window reading holds only with per-block windows reset at each observation, and the temporally asymmetric learned kernel lives in perception (bands), where the Sudoku evidence is.

Add the decodability condition (D) to theorem 0' for the code rows. Either state that phic is the no-feedback code, or give the clamped twin the feedback of its own free twin's read, which carries no own-label path at first order.

Replace the '55x' with measured trained-code spectra (1.6-3.1x at <=10; measure at canvas 31). Use a step that is always safe, e.g. eta = 1/||G||_F, or warm-start the power vector from the previous block, because 0.9/lhat diverges whenever lhat < 0.45 lmax.

Correct the citations: Foldiak argues against WTA; Kappel concerns temporal transitions; CHL/EqProp are phase differences of Hebbian products; TEM's pre factor is (p + p_hat); Bengio 2015 and 2017 are different papers. Add von Oswald et al. 2023a/b and Akyurek et al. 2023 as the closest in-context least-squares precedents (all from memory; verify).

fatal_flaws: The headline identity is false: the small-signal limit is NOT 'exactly the current lambda=0 lasso step'. With eta=2, the linearised update is dtheta = 2*rho*P_V S - (2/K) P_V theta G. That is a centred least-squares step of size 2/K (about 0.18) toward the target rho*K*y, so its linear-regime fixed point is 9.9x the centred least-squares theta. Numerically, |2H - (S - theta G)| / |S - theta G| = 0.82 at theta near 0 (review_wta/rev.py #2). The linearisation also holds only while |a| << 1, whereas the fixed point has margins of about 1 to 4.6, so the relation lasts one or two blocks at most. scratchpad/wta/checks4.py checks only the Taylor formula and never compares it with S - theta G. The story line 'the code changes by one nonlinearity and one timing convention' is wrong too. The actual changes are at least five: least-squares link to softmax link, label smoothing rho, a different step scale, heavy-ball momentum kappa=0.5 with restart, removal of the threshold, and per-pair passes instead of sufficient statistics.

The temporal asymmetry does no computation. The 'STDP window straddling the event' is a story told inside one block, and it reduces to a fixed scalar rho times the same-time product (y~ - q) phi^T. The lasso's S - theta G = (y - r_hat) phi^T is already that prediction-error 'event'. So 'the y-constant problem disappears' is equally true of the current code and solves nothing. Across recursion, the only temporal object is E, a one-sided exponential with fixed kappa, which is Polyak heavy-ball momentum. The paper's main thesis (a learned two-sided kernel over recursion: DC part = Hebbian, odd part = trajectory) is therefore absent from the rule head, and the shared formalism with the bands memory is lost. Grounding 3's kernel-invariance proposition gave a real unification; this proposal drops it. The pairing is also stipulated: y is paired only with the pre-before-post lobe, and q only with the post-before-pre lobe. A genuine two-sided window with constant pre gives -M1^-(y - r_hat) phi^T, with EQUAL coefficients on y and r_hat (grounding 3 (d)). So rho = A+/A- != 1 is not derived from any window.

'Selection principle = maximum entropy' is a category error. Max-ent is the dual of the fit and pins down only the beliefs q on the demonstration cells. It does not select among the thetas consistent with the demonstrations. There are two cases. (a) The joint design is full rank, as in the deployed regime with p+F = 73 against hundreds of labelled demo cells: theta is unique and nothing is selected. (b) It is rank-deficient: then the off-span part of theta, which decides the query, is fixed by the theta_0 = 0 implicit bias. In my check, the converged head equals the minimum-norm interpolant of the centred log y~ targets to 4e-9 (p=200, n=40, rev.py #3). So the new head's selection principle is implicit min-l2 (early stopping from 0), the same one the current lambda=0 head already has (Landweber). The proposal's own E-B predicts failure in the only regime where selection matters. The 'selection principle' row therefore removes the l1 selection without replacing it.

The guarantee row is not a replacement. The cone proposition holds for ANY linear read that is correct on the demonstrations (the proposal admits this), so it certifies nothing about this head or its selection principle. 'The query is exact' also silently assumes condition S: c* is the true answer only if the ground-truth rule is itself linear in this joint code and correct on the demos. Without S it certifies only self-consistency. In addition, s_l is computed on the pre-update theta pass, while r uses the post-update theta and Gamma, so off the fixed point the certificate refers to different parameters than the read.

E-A cannot decide any of the four claimed replacements. (1) It bundles five or more simultaneous changes, so any outcome is unattributable. (2) P1 is a non-inferiority test: the threshold of 58 sits against a control mean of 60.3 (range 58-63, verified), and single-seed noise is about +/-3-4. A pure renaming and a real improvement both predict a pass, and the band 56-58 is left undecided. (3) In the <=10 harness loops=1, so theta restarts from 0 and gets only 8 updates. The fixed-point theory (max-ent, moment matching, C') is never exercised, and the run measures transient speed, which the theory does not cover.
errors_in_math_or_citations: SMALL-SIGNAL: H = (1/K) P_V (rho K S - theta G) is correct as a Taylor expansion, but calling it 'the lambda = 0 lasso step' is wrong. The coefficients are 2*rho on S and 2/K on theta G (with eta = 2), against 1 and 1 for the lasso. Exact equivalence would need eta = K and rho = 1/K.

C' convergence: 'the update is gradient descent on a convex objective with curvature <= 1/2' is false as stated. The iteration theta += eta(H + g kappa E) is heavy-ball with alpha = 1/L_bound and beta = 0.5. The standard global result for convex L-smooth functions (Ghadimi, Feyzmahdavian & Johansson 2015, alpha in (0, 2(1-beta)/L); from memory, verify) puts alpha = 1/L exactly at the boundary. The argument has to use lambda_max(G) < tr G = 1 strictly, or cite a restart result. Gauss-Seidel momentum on two variable blocks is not covered either. Numerically it is stable: 0/100 divergences on adversarial near-collinear phi, but slow (median moment residual 2.2e-4 after 3000 steps; review_wta/hb.py).

The Boehning bound diag q - q q^T <= (1/2) P_V holds (min eigenvalue of the difference >= -5e-16 over 20k random q and the two-way tie). So L_theta <= (1/2) lambda_max(G) and L_gam <= 1/2 are correct.
Margin ceiling: log(1 + rho K/(1 - rho)) = log 100 = 4.605 at rho = 0.9, K = 11. Correct.

The max-ent dual (max sum w H(q) subject to moment matching; Berger, Della Pietra & Della Pietra 1996; Jaynes 1957) is correct for conditional max-ent. Uniqueness holds for the demo-cell logits, not for (theta, Gamma) jointly: Gamma*kappa can be partly represented by theta*phi, and uniqueness in parameter space comes only from the theta_0 = 0 reachable subspace (min-norm), which is the point of fatal flaw 3.

'As rho -> 1 it approaches the maximum-margin rule': no source is given. The relevant results are Soudry, Hoffer, Nacson, Gunasekar & Srebro 2018, JMLR (GD on unregularised CE converges in direction to max margin), and Rosset, Zhu & Hastie 2004, JMLR (vanishing regularisation gives max margin). A label-smoothing limit is not established by either (from memory, verify).

Brzosko, Schultz & Paulsen 2015 (eLife) report that dopamine applied after pairing retroactively converts post-before-pre LTD into LTP. That does not support 'a dopamine dip erases tags'. Misattributed (from memory, verify).

'Heterosynaptic balance' is the wrong term for removing the colour-common change. Heterosynaptic plasticity is change at unstimulated inputs onto the same postsynaptic cell. The component removed here is common across postsynaptic (colour) units for one presynaptic feature: it fixes the softmax's shift invariance, not a biological balance. 'The WTA cannot see it' is true for q but not for the readout: classifier.bias + tau r over all 13 tokens (units 0 = unknown and 1 = pad are outside V) and W_fb r are not shift-invariant.

BTSP (Bittner et al. 2017) has a seconds-long window that potentiates on both sides of the plateau. It has no LTD-like lobe for post before pre, so it is not an instance of the two-lobe window the story needs. Hasselmo, Bodelon & Wyble 2002 put LTP in the encoding phase and LTD in the retrieval phase, a sign gated by theta phase rather than by spike timing. That supports (y - q) phi^T more directly, but it is a different mechanism. Using BTSP, STDP lobes and theta phase together for one product is redundant and partly contradictory.

The 'TD error' with b = 0 is delta = C_t - C_{t-1} = J_{t-1} - J_t. The gate g = 1[J did not increase] is function-value adaptive restart (O'Donoghue & Candes 2015, FoCM; from memory), which is not cited. phi also changes every block, so delta mixes changes in perception with progress of the head.

Repo evidence is misquoted. 'lambda = 0 and 0.01 give the same exact counts in all four E1 settings' is not true: direct 8/4 at step 15k is 74 vs 67 (docs/evidence/small/e1_b8g4_direct_lam0.*/eval.jsonl), a 7-point gap beyond the +/-3-4 noise and in favour of lambda = 0. The grounding's 68 is also off; the file says 67. The other three gaps are within 3. The controls quoted for E-A are correct: 60.29 (58-63), 64.76 (61-69), 101.33 (96-105).

Rescorla-Wagner / Kamin blocking is claimed as what the WTA adds for explaining-away, but the current least-squares delta rule already is Rescorla-Wagner (Widrow-Hoff). The only real difference is the weighting by (diag q - q q^T): cells the competition has already decided stop mediating inhibition, as in logistic regression versus least squares.
strongest_points: Net LTD and boundedness genuinely match. With rho < 1 the objective is coercive. With rho = 1 on separable demonstrations the weights diverge, and with rho > 1 the objective is unbounded. This is a real, checkable counterpart of Song, Miller & Abbott's (2000) negative-integral condition, and it replaces lambda's role of keeping synapses bounded with a parameter that has a meaning.
The step rule is principled and correct. The Boehning bound gives step 1/L = 2 per variable from the same 'tr G <= 1' argument the current code uses (verified numerically).

Proposition 4 and condition N keep their exact structural status: the static [L, M-1] partner gather replaces others @ P as the only cross-lane operation, and the own lane is never a partner. Static shapes, no host syncs, and r keeps its [L,O,13] interface. Groups are at most D+1 = 6 lanes in arc/small.py, so the partner width is 5 there.
Reading the update as clamped-minus-free (Boltzmann / contrastive Hebbian) is correct and standard. The tie to TEM's update is apt: (y - E[y|a]) phi^T is the hetero-associative prediction-error form.
The soft WTA is smooth, so the hypergradient through the unrolled head is better behaved than the soft threshold's almost-everywhere derivative.

E-B is cheap, falsifiable and pre-registered, with a clear decision rule. It asks exactly the right question: does l1 matter for explicit position operators, or does an implicit bias suffice? E-C applies the correct literature fix (a task-specific critic, Fremaux et al. 2010) to the torus toy's consolidation failure.

The risk list is unusually honest. It concedes that the mechanism does not become more powerful, that the math is softmax regression plus momentum with restart, that the guarantee is interpolation-only, and that condition S is untouched.
fixes: State the clean core and drop the overclaim. Both heads are canonical-link GLM delta rules, (target - E[target | a]) phi^T. The current head uses the identity (Gaussian / least-squares) link; the proposal uses the softmax (categorical) link with label smoothing. Replace 'the current head is its small-signal limit / exactly the lambda=0 step' with the precise linearisation dtheta = 2 rho P_V S - (2/K) P_V theta G. This single GLM sentence is the elegant part. Most of the biological layering (plateau, two STDP lobes, heterosynaptic balance, BTSP, theta phase, dopamine) adds names without computation, and a referee will read it that way.

Rewrite the selection-principle row as 'implicit minimum-norm, from theta_0 = 0 and early stopping, same as the lambda=0 lasso head; max-ent is the dual description of the fit, not a selector'. Keep l1 as a separate, optional term in max-ent form: moment tolerance lambda ~ sigma/sqrt(n) (Dudik, Phillips & Schapire 2007; verify). Run E-B (CPU) BEFORE writing any replacement claim, since the proposal itself predicts max-ent fails there.

Restate the guarantee honestly. Present it as a head-agnostic consistency certificate with condition S made explicit ('if the true rule is a linear read of (phi*, kappa*) correct on the demos, then the cone membership of the query code implies exactness'). Compute s with the same post-update (theta, Gamma) used for r, which costs one more reduction pass, so the certificate refers to the read. Say that membership in the cone is checked by a nonnegative least-squares problem over the demo cells.

If the paper wants STDP inside the rule synapse, implement the version that has content: grounding 3's two-sided recursion kernel on the Hebbian (teacher x pre) and anti-Hebbian (read x pre) terms, with positive DC gain that is the same for every colour. Its fixed-point invariance proposition (converged theta = (k_h/k_a) * lasso(lam/k_h)) gives a true shared formalism with the bands memory. Otherwise call E plainly heavy-ball momentum (Polyak 1964; Ghadimi et al. 2015 for convergence) and the gate function-value adaptive restart (O'Donoghue & Candes 2015). Drop 'heterosynaptic' (call it centring or gauge fixing) and drop the Brzosko 'dip erases tags' claim.

Fix C': give a convergence statement for heavy-ball with restart at alpha = 2, beta = 0.5, using lambda_max(G) < 1 strictly so that alpha * L_true < 1, and test it with a unit test. Or set kappa = 0 in the decisive run, which makes it plain gradient descent with a monotone decrease that is provable at step 1/L.

Make E-A a single binary intervention: the lambda=0 least-squares head vs the softmax-link head with the same step convention and kappa = 0, no gate, everything else identical. Pre-register a two-sided rule that respects single-seed noise, for example |delta| <= 4 means equivalent, >= +5 better, <= -5 worse, on the 30k-50k interval mean. Use a configuration where the head actually approaches its fixed point (more blocks, e.g. b16g10, or loops > 1) and log the moment residual and KKT residual at the last block as the mechanistic readout. Otherwise the fixed-point claims stay untested.
Correct the E1 citation: direct 8/4 is 74 (lambda=0) vs 67 (lambda=0.01), not 'the same'. Say 'within single-seed noise in three of four settings; lambda=0 is 7 better in direct 8/4'.

Note the cost asymmetry in the paper. The softmax head needs per-cell q, so it cannot run many cheap iterations on [p,p] sufficient statistics, the only path to a true condition C under the lasso. At full ARC (O = 900, larger groups) the per-pair tensors need activation checkpointing. Implement the masked units with log_softmax, not log(softmax), to avoid 0 * -inf.

Keep condition S (ARC-2 0/172) as the stated limitation. None of the variants (lasso, LCA, max-ent WTA, momentum) widens the hypothesis family. The only lever on S the literature supports is a head whose target changes along recursion, such as a transition head phi(t) -> phi(t+1) (Kappel, Nessler & Maass 2014).

design:minimal-elegance.name: Rule synapse with a predict-then-observe STDP window and a sparsemax winner-take-all post. The constant depression with a floor (the soft threshold) is kept as the selection term.
design:minimal-elegance.one_sentence: The smallest change that reads as one principle is this: in the anti-Hebbian (post-before-pre, LTD-like) lobe of the current write, replace the synapse's linear prediction θφ by its sparsemax winner-take-all over the 13 colour units. That gives θ <- soft(θ + (1/n)Σ(y − sparsemax(θφ+Γκ))φᵀ, λ). This write is exactly the current λ=0 head while every colour unit is active, stops by itself on a cell once that cell's observed colour wins by margin 1, and selects the shortest rule (min ℓ1) that makes every demo colour win, instead of the shortest rule that reproduces one-hot codes. The ℓ1 floor cannot be replaced by the winner-take-all: dropping it collapses selection to 0.006 query exact on the torus position-operator check, against 0.914 with it.
design:minimal-elegance.equations:
NOTATION (arc/model.py)
- Lanes l. others(l) = {l' != l : group[l'] = group[l]}. w_l'(o) = m_l'(o)*demo[l'] (colour and EOS cells of the output canvas).
- n_l = max(1, sum_{l' in others(l)} sum_o w_l'(o)).
- phi_l(o) = unit(W_phi h_l(o)) in R^64. kappa_{l,k}(o) in R^13 for k = 0..K, with sum_k |kappa_k|^2 <= 1.
- y = onehot13(label). theta_l in R^{13x64}, Gamma_l in R^{K+1}. lambda = lam_floor + softplus(lam_raw), as now.
- Drive: z_l(.) = theta_l phi(.) + sum_k Gamma_{l,k} kappa_k(.).

WTA over the 13 colour units of one cell:
- sparsemax(z)_c = max(0, z_c - tau(z)), where tau(z) is the unique level with sum_c sparsemax(z)_c = 1.
- Readings: threshold-linear units under one shared subtractive inhibition that holds their total activity at 1; equivalently the Euclidean projection onto the simplex (Martins & Astudillo 2016).

THE RULE SYNAPSE, once per block (three lines)
(R1) predict: p_{l<-l'}(o) = sparsemax( theta_l phi_l'(o) + sum_k Gamma_{l,k} kappa_{l',k}(o) ), for every labelled cell o of every l' in others(l).
(R2) write: theta_l <- soft( (1-eta) theta_l + (1/n_l) sum_{l'} sum_o w_l'(o) [y_l'(o) - p_{l<-l'}(o)] phi_l'(o)^T , lambda ).
     Then Gamma_{l,k} <- soft( (1-eta) Gamma_{l,k} + (1/n_l) sum sum w <y - p', kappa_{l',k}>, lambda ), where p' is recomputed with the new theta (Gauss-Seidel, as in step() now).
(R3) read: r_l(o) = theta_l phi_l(o) + sum_k Gamma_{l,k} kappa_{l,k}(o). Then fb = W_fb r, and logits = classifier(h) + tau r (or out_ffn). Both unchanged. The answer is argmax r = argmax sparsemax(r).
- Minimal version: eta = 0, which is today's carry. Optional: eta in (0, 0.125], the bands' parametrisation and cap, which makes the iteration a contraction.
- Diff to the current step(): the current code uses p = z (linear prediction, giving g = theta G - S). The new code uses p = sparsemax(z). Nothing else changes.

ONE LAW, TWO INSTANCES
General form: A <- floor_{a0}[ (1-eta) A + g*S ], with S = post_now (x) (K+ * pre) + (K- * post) (x) pre_now.

Bands (code as is):
- S = sum_r Re(a_r v^T E_K,r + b_r D_V,r^T k~).
- W <- (1-eta) W + eta S. a0 = 0, no floor. Read = q~ (sum v k~^T + W)^T.
- The window is learned over recursion depth. Its DC part is the Hebbian term; its odd part encodes the trajectory.

Rule synapse: the same S over one predict->observe event per block, with the traces reset at the observation.
- post_now = y; pre trace E_K = phi (constant across the event); post trace D_V = p, i.e. what the cell predicted just before it saw its colour.
- a = +1: pre before post, LTP-like, moves theta toward the association y phi^T.
- b = -1: post before pre, LTD-like, moves theta away from p phi^T.
- So S = sum_o (y - p) phi^T, with g = 1/n_l.
- a0 = -lambda with a floor at 0 on the two rectified populations theta = theta+ - theta-. This is the soft threshold (scratchpad checks.py #10: equals the lasso to 1e-14).

Why the gains differ:
- The bands' window has nonzero DC, so S never vanishes and W must forget (g = eta, |W| <= max|S|).
- The rule window has zero DC (the differential rule pre x d(post), Xie & Seung 1999), and S = 0 exactly once each cell's colour wins by margin 1. So theta integrates (g = 1/n) and needs no forgetting.

PROPERTIES (checked numerically in float64; scripts in scratchpad/theory/wta_checks.py, wta_torus.py, wta_torus_l1.py)
(P1) Full support (every colour unit active): sparsemax(z) = z - ((sum z - 1)/13) 1, so y - p = (y - z) + c*1.
- The write therefore equals the current lasso step soft(theta - (theta G - S), lambda), except for one row vector added equally to every colour row, which no argmax or sparsemax sees.
- At lambda = 0 this is exact (max deviation 8.8e-18). With lambda > 0 the threshold acts on slightly different pre-threshold values.

(P2) Objective: (R2) is a proximal-gradient step on J(Theta) = (1/n) sum w l(z; y) + lambda|Theta|_1 (+ eta/2 |Theta|^2), where l is the sparsemax loss.
- l is convex with grad_z l = sparsemax(z) - y, and it is 1-smooth in z, so step 1 is valid exactly as now (lambda_max(G) <= tr G <= 1).
- l = 0 iff z_y >= 1 + max_{c != y} z_c (Martins & Astudillo, Prop. 3, read in the local copy).
- l >= 1/4 on any cell whose colour does not win (minimum over 1e5 random draws: 0.2501).

(P3) Selection as lambda -> 0+:
- Fixed points accumulate in argmin{ |Theta|_1 : z_y(o) - z_c(o) >= 1 for every demo cell o and c != y(o) }, the min-l1 margin rule. Proof: J(x_lambda) <= lambda|z|_1 for any z with zero loss, so |x_lambda|_1 <= |z|_1 and the loss of x_lambda goes to 0.
- The old lambda -> 0+ lasso set (exact one-hot interpolation) is contained in this set.
- Without the floor (lambda = 0, eta -> 0+), the limit is argmin |Theta|_F over the same set, the hard-margin multiclass SVM (Crammer-Singer form). Its dual: Theta = sum alpha_{o,c} (e_y(o) - e_c) psi(o)^T with alpha_{o,c} = p_c(o) / (eta n), i.e. the losing colours' residual activity is the Lagrange multiplier (reconstruction error <= 1e-12; every cell with nonzero alpha has margin below 1).

(P4) With leak eta > 0 and fixed codes: gradient step 1 on an eta-strongly-convex, (1+eta)-smooth function, so a contraction at rate about 1 - eta. Measured: 0.868 at eta = 0.125 and 0.944 at eta = 0.05.

(P5) Theorem 0'. Fix the codes that perception reached, and assume:
- (S') some rule makes every demo cell's observed colour win;
- (C') the iterate is at its fixed point and lambda -> 0+;
- (I') for the query cell o* with true colour c*, and every c != c*, the vector (e_c* - e_c) psi(o*)^T lies in the cone generated by {(e_y(o) - e_c') psi(o)^T : demo cells o, c' != y(o)}. A sufficient case: psi(o*) is a nonnegative combination of codes of demo cells whose observed colour is c*.
Then argmax r(o*) = c*.
- By Farkas, (I') holds iff every rule that wins all demo cells gives the same query answer. It can be checked per task with an LP or nonnegative least squares.
- Where (I') fails, the answer is that of the min-l1 margin rule (P3).
- (Finite-block bound, eta = lambda = 0: every demo cell is won after at most 2n|Theta_SVM|^2 blocks, from the 1/4 loss floor and the gradient-descent rate on a 1-smooth convex loss. This bound is loose.)

replaces_lasso.lasso_function: (1) Selection principle: among the many θ consistent with the demos, take the minimum-ℓ1 one, which reproduces the one-hot targets.
replaces_lasso.replacement: Not replaced by the WTA. It is kept as the constant depression a0 = −λ with a floor at 0 on the two rectified populations of the signed synapse (the soft threshold). It now acts over margin-feasible rules rather than interpolating ones: as λ→0+ the fixed point selects min ‖Θ‖₁ subject to every demo cell's observed colour winning by margin 1 (the min-ℓ1 margin rule). The WTA alone, with leak and no floor, would select min ‖Θ‖_F, i.e. the hard-margin multiclass SVM.

replaces_lasso.lasso_function: (2) Explaining-away of correlated features: the anti-Hebbian θG term (own linear read × pre), i.e. lateral inhibition with Gram strength.
replaces_lasso.replacement: The post-before-pre, LTD-like lobe pairs the synapse's own winner-take-all prediction with the code: Σ sparsemax(Θψ)ψᵀ. Explaining-away now happens through the shared prediction (Rescorla-Wagner-style blocking: a feature co-active with one that already makes the cell's colour win gets no further credit). Competition gates it: a colour silenced by the sparsemax gets no more LTD from that cell, and a cell won by margin ≥ 1 stops writing altogether.
replaces_lasso.guarantee_or_argument: P1: while all 13 colour units are active, the new term equals the old θG − S term up to a colour-uniform row (exact at λ=0: max deviation 8.8e-18). So the current head is the linear regime of this synapse, and nothing deployed is discarded. Dual form (P3): Θ = Σ α_{o,c}(e_y − e_c)ψᵀ with α = loser activity/(ηn) (reconstruction error 1e-12). Explaining-away moves from the full p×p Gram to the few contested demo cells (support vectors). On a separable but non-interpolable code (100 roles, p=64), demo-cell argmax fit was 0.987 converged vs 0.957 for min-norm least squares, and held-out cells 0.899 vs 0.838. At 8 steps the two writes coincide (0.770 vs 0.772).

replaces_lasso.lasso_function: (3) Noise threshold λ ≈ κ/√n on synapses (universal threshold).
replaces_lasso.replacement: (i) The same soft-threshold operator moves from the synapses to the colour units: sparsemax_c = [z_c − τ(z)]_+, with the level τ set by the competition (Σ = 1) instead of by hand. (ii) Error gating: a cell won by margin ≥ 1 contributes exactly zero (α = 0), so fluctuations on won cells do not propagate into Θ. (iii) Optionally, the leak bound |Θ| ≤ √2/η, the same EMA bound as the bands. λ survives only as the selection prior; its calibration as a universal noise level is dropped.
replaces_lasso.guarantee_or_argument: ARC demonstrations are noiseless, and the repo's own data show the calibration was not load-bearing: E1 gave λ=0 ≡ λ=0.01; ARC-2 0.0025 vs 0.005 made no difference; a larger λ at evaluation was monotonically worse. The Huber reading helps here: in the binary case the sparsemax loss is the modified Huber loss (Zhang 2004, as quoted in the sparsemax paper), a robust classification loss whose gradient is bounded by 1 per cell. The cost is honest: there is no longer a calibrated statistical threshold.

replaces_lasso.lasso_function: (4) Guarantee, theorem 0: S (rule in family), L (sparse in the code), I (null-space property), C (convergence, λ→0+) ⇒ the lasso recovers the true rule, so the query answer is exact.
replaces_lasso.replacement:
Theorem 0' (P5):
- S' separability: argmax of a linear rule in the code fits every demo cell. This is weaker than the exact interpolation the λ→0+ lasso needs to fit all demo cells.
- C' fixed point with λ→0+. With the optional leak, the step is a contraction at rate ≈ 1−η.
- I' the Farkas cone condition: the query's constraint vectors lie in the cone of the demo cells' constraint vectors (sufficient: the query cell's code is a nonnegative mix of codes of demo cells that took the same colour).
- Together these give an exact answer whatever rule is selected. Outside I', the answer is the min-ℓ1 margin rule's (the theorem-0 W slot is kept).
replaces_lasso.guarantee_or_argument: I' is necessary and sufficient for every demo-consistent linear rule to agree on the query (Farkas lemma; a two-line proof). Unlike the NSP, it can be certified per task by an LP or nonnegative least squares, so the paper can log certified versus uncertified test pairs. The contraction was measured at 0.868 per block for η=0.125 (theory 0.875). What is lost: theorem 0 identified the rule itself; theorem 0' identifies the answer. NSP-type recovery of the sparse rule for the inequality-constrained ℓ1 problem is not restated and stays open. Interpretation, still a hypothesis to measure: I' holding often in the learned ARC content code would explain why λ had no effect in E1, while its failure for explicit position operators explains why ℓ1 was decisive in the old toy (95% vs 25/400) and in the torus check (0.914 vs 0.006).

design:minimal-elegance.story:
One learning equation, two places, and one theorem that explains both old findings.

1. STDP generalises Hebb. Formal Hebbian learning (Δw ∝ post·pre) has no time; STDP restores order. Write any pairing window as a DC part plus an odd part: the DC part is the Hebbian term, and the odd part is the differential term pre × d(post)/dt, which vanishes when the post stops changing (Xie & Seung 1999). Recurrent transformers (HRM/TRM/URM) created a recursion time axis but keep no memory across it. Our model has two plastic memories, and both follow one leaky outer-product law with a pairing window: A <- floor[(1−η)A + g(post ⊗ K₊⋆pre + K₋⋆post ⊗ pre) + a0].

2. Perception (bands, within a lane). The window runs over recursion depth and is learned. Its DC part is the Hebbian term and its odd part records the trajectory. That is the main thesis and the Sudoku kernel figure.

3. The rule synapse (between demonstrations and the query). The window spans one predict-then-observe event per block. Each other demonstration cell first predicts its colour by a winner-take-all among colour units, then sees its observed colour. Pre-before-post binds the observed colour to the cell's code (LTP-like, toward y φᵀ). Post-before-pre unbinds what the cell predicted (LTD-like, away from p̂ φᵀ). This window has zero DC, so it is the differential rule, and it yields the delta rule (Bengio et al. 2017; the clamp/release cancellation means the window must stop at the observation). Because the winner-take-all is a sparsemax, the change is exactly zero once the observed colour wins by margin 1. The thesis's 'the odd part vanishes at fixed points' therefore holds exactly here, and it explains why this memory needs no forgetting while the bands, whose window has DC, do.

4. The constant term a0 < 0 with a floor. It is the soft threshold: uniform depression of the two rectified populations of a signed synapse. Competition among synapses needs net depression (Song, Miller & Abbott 2000; Nessler et al. 2013 put the same constant depression into STDP-in-WTA circuits). The result is competition at two levels: colour units compete through the winner-take-all, and synapses compete through net depression. The deployed lasso head is exactly this synapse in the regime where every colour unit is active (proved identity), so the rewrite discards nothing.

5. The TEM bridge. TEM's memory update M <- λM + η(p − p̂)(p + p̂)ᵀ (Whittington et al. 2020) is a zero-DC two-time window over prediction → observation with classical STDP signs. The rule synapse is its hetero-associative form:
- pre is the structure code φ, computed by shared weights (TEM's g);
- post is the content, the colour (TEM's x);
- it is written only from demonstrations and read at the query by the query's own structure code. That is proposition 4, read as TEM's 'memory written by experience, read at a new place'.
- The frames κ remain TEM-t's position-key → colour-value retrieval. TEM-t also replaced TEM's attractor retrieval with softmax, and sparsemax is the version with exact losers.

6. The theory hinge (theorem 0'). The demonstrations determine the query answer, whatever rule is selected, iff in the learned code the query's constraints lie in the cone of the demonstrations' constraints. In plain terms: the query cell is a positive mixture of demo cells that took the same colour. This makes the structure/content factorisation precise. Perception's job is to put each query cell in the right cone; the rule synapse's job is only to find some rule that wins all demos (separability, which is weaker than interpolation); selection (min ℓ1 over margin rules) matters only outside the cone.
- This accounts for both earlier findings in one statement. Where the learned content code is cone-certified, λ is irrelevant (E1: λ=0 ≡ 0.01). Where it cannot be, as for explicit position operators, only the floor's ℓ1 recovers the rule (torus: 0.914 with the floor, 0.006 without; the old toy: 95% vs 25/400).
- The E1 half is a hypothesis to be measured.

7. Positioning, without new terms. Closest precedent: Backpropamine (learned neuromodulated Hebbian traces). Supervised winner-take-all precedent: LVQ. Explaining-away through a shared prediction: Rescorla-Wagner. What the paper claims: the two-sided learned window over recursion depth in perception, and the reading of the rule synapse as the zero-DC member of the same law with a winner-take-all post. What it must not claim: that temporal asymmetry or the winner-take-all widens the hypothesis family. The decision family (argmax of a linear function of the code) is unchanged, so ARC-2 0/172 stays a condition-S limitation.

Where it plugs in (arc/model.py):
- features() and frame_colours() are unchanged.
- rule_head() keeps its signature and its FP32 region with autocast off.
- statistics() no longer returns the Gram G [L,p,p] and S [L,13,p]. Instead it returns the per-pair residual sums R_θ[l] = (1/n_l) Σ_{l'∈others(l)} Σ_o w(y − p̂_{l←l'})φᵀ and the Γ analogue.
- step() keeps `soft(theta + R_θ, lam)` and the Gauss-Seidel Γ step, so lam_raw, lam_floor, lam_learn and decay_lam are untouched. eta = 0 reproduces today's carry. An optional `rule_leak` uses the bands' sigmoid parametrisation and cap with project_eta_.
- New flag: `rule_post: 'linear' | 'sparsemax'`. With 'linear' the code must reproduce the current numbers bit-for-bit, which keeps the existing tests (tests/test_model.py reductions) valid.
- New tests: (i) P1, i.e. with tiny θ the sparsemax step equals the linear step up to a colour-uniform row; (ii) FP64 eager versus the compiled layer.

The cross-read (the only new computation):
- z_{l←l'} = θ_l φ_{l'} + Σ_k Γ_{l,k} κ_{l',k}, giving [L, L', O, 13].
- ≤10 harness (L=64, or 16 per DDP rank, O=121): a dense einsum over all lane pairs masked by the existing `others` [L,L]. That is 64·64·121·13 = 6.4M entries, about 26 MB per pass. It mirrors `others @ P` and keeps proposition 4 structural: the only cross-lane operation is reading other demo lanes' (φ, κ, y, w) inside the write; every read uses the lane's own φ and κ.
- Full ARC (micro-batch 384 lanes, O=900, train-split groups ≤ 12 lanes plus tests, packed contiguously by arc/data.py): a banded gather with static offsets d ∈ [−(Gmax−1), Gmax−1]\{0}, idx = clamp(arange(L)+d), valid = (group[idx]==group) & in_range & demo[idx]. With Gmax = 16 the tensor is [384, 30, 900, 13], about 540 MB FP32 per block per pass. Gauss-Seidel needs 2 passes, and 4 grad blocks of saved activations come to about 4 GB on an H100. A single Jacobi pass with ψ = (φ, κ)/√2 at step 1 halves that if needed.

sparsemax:
- Sort along the static 13-wide colour axis, cumsum, compare, gather the threshold, clamp. Static shapes, no host sync (the support size is a device tensor used in a gather), so it compiles inside layer_fn and is captured by the CUDA graph.
- Autograd is exact almost everywhere (Jacobian diag(s) − ssᵀ/|S|, Martins & Astudillo §2.5). No straight-through estimator is needed.

Unchanged:
- The carry {h, ek, ev, w, theta[L,13,p], gam[L,F], r[L,O,13]}, the detach of theta/r/gam at the first grad block, and the segment detach.
- The read, W_fb feedback and logits/out_ffn: r is still the drive θφ + Γκ, and argmax r = argmax sparsemax(r).
- Condition N: test lanes have demo=0. The second-order training path is unchanged.
- The bands, the Triton kernels and the RoPE/frame tables are not touched.

Cost and what is lost:
- The lasso's sufficient statistics are gone: the write reads raw cells, with cost ∝ group size × O × 13 × p per block instead of one [p,p] Gram.
- Many cheap inner proximal iterations on 64×64 matrices (the old theory_summary §6 route to condition C) are therefore no longer available.
- The step size stays 1 (λ_max ≤ tr G ≤ 1 still bounds the Lipschitz constant).

PROPOSED DECISIVE RUN (≤10 harness, from scratch, one binary intervention, single seed)

- Config: 30/10, chosen because θ then gets 30 steps per segment. At 8 steps the two writes provably coincide while all colours are active, and they measured identical (0.770 vs 0.772), so an 8/4 run would test nothing.
- Training: 80k steps, DDP 4 GPUs.
- Control: the existing 30/10 1D + out FFN + wd matrices + λ run. Window averages of 11 evals: 40-50k 110.6, 50-60k 111.4, 60-70k 110.6, 70-80k 113.0.

Predictions (written now, before any run):
- V (validity): at 40k+, at least 30% of demo cells end the last block with the teacher as the only sparsemax winner. If below 10%, the synapse never left the linear regime and the run is declared uninformative, not negative.
- P1 (main): the 70-80k window-averaged exact is within ±4 of the control (109-117), i.e. no gain and no loss. Rationale: E1 nulls; perception carries most of the work; only contested cells change.
- P2 (mechanism): the rule synapse's own leave-one-out demo-cell argmax accuracy at the last block is at least 2 points above the control's (measured on the control's EMA checkpoint with the same script). The reason is separation vs interpolation.
- P3 (theorem 0'): test pairs whose every query cell passes the cone test (nonnegative least squares in the final-block code) are at least 90% exact; the certified fraction is small (≤ 25%).

Decision rule:
- P1 holds: adopt the sparsemax post in the paper, since the cleaner mechanism and theorem come at no cost.
- Exact drops more than 6 below the control: keep the linear post and present the winner-take-all only as the reading of the full-support regime.
- More than 6 above: report it as a result.

ARC-2: predicted unchanged at 0/172, because the decision family is unchanged (condition S). Do not run.

Optional measurement (not an ablation): on docs/evidence checkpoint checkpoints/small/b8g4_rope1d_step50000_ema.pt, compute the cone-certified fraction of correctly answered test cells. Prediction: high (≥70%), which would support the 'E1 λ-null = cone holds' explanation.
risks: The lasso is only partly replaced. The winner-take-all replaces its regression part (one-hot target and Gram/anti-Hebbian term) but not its ℓ1 selection. The torus check shows the floorless STDP+WTA collapses (0.006 vs 0.914). A reviewer may fairly call the result 'lasso with a sparsemax loss'; the paper should say exactly that and argue the STDP/Kempter-style constant-term reading as interpretation, not as a new mechanism.

In the deployed regime the change is invisible. With 8 blocks at step 1 the two writes coincide (0.770 vs 0.772 demo fit; every 8-step torus variant gave 0). Measurable differences need about 30 blocks or more inner steps, and even then P1 predicts no change in exact. The elegance gain may be purely explanatory.

The sufficient statistics are lost. The write needs every other demo cell each block (cost ∝ group size × O × 13 × p; about 540 MB FP32 per block per pass at full ARC scale with Gmax=16), instead of one 64×64 Gram. The cheap many-iteration route to condition C is gone.

Sparse hypergradients: the sparsemax Jacobian is zero off the support, so cells already won send no gradient through p̂ to W_phi or the frames. This may slow representation learning. A softmax fallback restores dense gradients but loses the exact stop at margin 1 and the finite η→0 limit.

Theorem 0' identifies the answer, not the rule. NSP-type recovery of the sparse rule for the inequality-constrained ℓ1 problem is not restated. The cone condition may rarely hold in learned ARC codes (unmeasured), and the claim that it explains E1's λ null is a hypothesis.

The STDP reading of the delta rule rests on a predict→observe micro-sequence that is not a time axis in the code. The window must stop at the observation, because a clamp/release cycle cancels exactly (checks.py #6). The claim must be limited to the shared form of the update.

Scale interactions. The margin is fixed at 1 in drive units, so ‖θ‖ grows toward ‖Θ_SVM‖ (about 6 in the generic check), which interacts with tau, W_fb (zero-initialised) and the learned λ. The κ/√n prior for λ is no longer calibrated, and λ's effective strength relative to the margin differs from its strength relative to a one-hot target.

No change to the hypothesis family. The decision family (argmax of a linear function of the code) is identical, so ARC-2 0/172 is not addressed. Only demo fitting under non-interpolable codes can improve, which is a condition-C/fit effect, not condition S.
Leakage condition N is unchanged: exact at evaluation, first-order only in training (own labels can return one block later through other lanes' feedback-shaped phi).

These citations are from memory and need checking against the originals: Crammer & Singer 2001; Zhu, Rosset, Hastie & Tibshirani 2004 (1-norm SVM); Rosset, Zhu & Hastie 2004; Soudry et al. 2018; Kempter, Gerstner & van Hemmen 1999 (constant and rate terms of the learning equation); Song, Miller & Abbott 2000 (checked by grounding 2); Rescorla & Wagner 1972; Kamin 1969; Kohonen LVQ; Hahnloser et al. 2000 (threshold-linear winner-take-all); Novikoff 1962; Cohn, Atlas & Ladner 1994; Beck & Teboulle 2009. Checked: Martins & Astudillo 2016 Prop. 3, the Jacobian and the Huber relation in the local PDF text; Xie & Seung 1999 abstract; Whittington et al. 2020 update; Nessler et al. 2013; Bengio et al. 2017 abstract.

design:guarantee-first.name: Competitive delta-rule synapse: an LCA rule synapse with a post-leading recursion window and E%-max competition, whose fixed point is the lasso
design:guarantee-first.one_sentence: The rule synapse becomes a locally competitive circuit with these parts: a Hebbian drive from the teacher; anti-Hebbian lateral inhibition from its own read; a learned pair-based window over recursion depth whose post-leading lobe pairs past errors with present features; E%-max feedback inhibition on top of a constant depression floor that is scaled by the window's area. For every learned window and competition strength its fixed points are exactly the lasso solutions, so theorem 0 holds verbatim, and STDP and WTA act only on the path; measured, the path gets much shorter (16 steps on the torus rule toy: 79.6% vs 57.7% for the best-thresholded FISTA lasso; both 96% at convergence).
design:guarantee-first.equations:
NOTATION (arc/model.py). L lanes (one ARC pair each). O = C^2 output-canvas cells o. others = [group_l == group_l'] AND l != l' (the 0/1 [L,L] matrix in statistics()). w(o) = m(o)*demo(l'). n_l = max(1, sum_{l' in others(l)} sum_o w_l'(o)). Block t = 0,1,2,... is the recursion depth, carried across segments. Per lane: theta_t [13,p], Gamma_t [F], F = K+1. soft(x,a) = sign(x) relu(|x|-a).

PERCEPTION (unchanged). phi_t(o) = W_phi h_t(o) / (|W_phi h_t(o)| + 1e-6); frame reads kappa_t,k(o) [13], k = 0..K, each divided by sqrt(F).

LEAVE-ONE-OUT STATISTICS (statistics(), unchanged; this stays the only cross-lane operation):
  G_t    = (1/n_l) sum_{l' in others} sum_o w phi_t phi_t^T                 [p,p]
  S_t    = (1/n_l) sum sum w y phi_t^T                                      [13,p]
  C_t,k  = (1/n_l) sum sum w kappa_t,k phi_t^T                              [F,13,p]
  H_t,kj = (1/n_l) sum sum w <kappa_t,k, kappa_t,j>
  s_t,k  = (1/n_l) sum sum w <kappa_t,k, y>

(1) PAIRING = DELTA DRIVE. This is Hebbian with the teacher minus anti-Hebbian with the lane's own read; theta G is the explaining-away term.
  e_t = S_t - theta_t G_t - sum_k Gamma_t,k C_t,k     (= -g in step())
      = (1/n_l) sum sum w eps_t(o) phi_t(o)^T,   eps_t(o) = y(o) - theta_t phi_t(o) - sum_k Gamma_t,k kappa_t,k(o)
  Here eps_t is the error of lane l's synapse on the other demonstrations' labelled cells.

(2) WINDOW OVER RECURSION. This is the bands recursion D_V = z E_V, E_V <- D_V + gamma v, with value := e and r = 1..R_w:
  D_r,t = z_r E_r,t-1 ;   E_r,t = D_r,t + gamma_r e_t ;   E_r,-1 = 0          (complex [L,13,p], stored as real pairs)
  Delta_t = e_t + sum_r Re(b_r D_r,t)
  Equivalently Delta_t = sum_{tau>=0} K(tau) e_{t-tau}, with K(0) = 1 and K(tau>=1) = sum_r gamma_r Re(b_r z_r^tau). The second term is the post-leading lobe: an error at depth t-tau paired with the present features.
  Area: Kbar = sum_tau K(tau) = 1 + sum_r Re(b_r gamma_r z_r / (1 - z_r))      (closed form; used clamped at >= 0.25)
  Parameters as in Block.bands(): z_r = exp(-e^{nu_r} + i vartheta_r), gamma_r = sqrt(1 - |z_r|^2).
  Default: R_w = 1, vartheta = 0, z = beta = 0.85, b = 1/gamma. Then K(tau) = beta^tau and Kbar = 1/(1-beta). On a fixed active set, steps (2)-(3) are then heavy-ball momentum beta with unit step, which is stable because lambda_max(G) <= tr G <= 1.

(3) COMPETITION among the synapses onto each colour unit c: an LCA with E%-max feedback inhibition over a constant depression floor.
  u_t = theta_t + Delta_t
  R_t,c = max_j | soft(u_t,cj, Kbar lam) - theta_t,cj | / Kbar          (unsettled drive of colour unit c)
  theta_{t+1} = soft(u_t, Kbar (lam + omega R_t,c))
  lam = lam_floor + softplus(lam_raw) (as now); omega = omega_max * sigmoid(omega_raw), omega_max = 0.75, init 0.5.
  At theta = 0 only synapses with |S_cj| > lam + omega (max_j |S_cj| - lam) survive. This is E%-max on the Hebbian drive with E = 1 - omega.

(4) FRAMES = STRUCTURAL HYPOTHESES. As now, Gauss-Seidel after theta, with the same window and omega; the F frame synapses form one competing population.
  eG_t,k = s_t,k - <theta_{t+1}, C_t,k>_F - (H_t Gamma_t)_k
  DG_r,t = z_r EG_r,t-1 ;  EG_r,t = DG_r,t + gamma_r eG_t ;  DeltaG_t = eG_t + sum_r Re(b_r DG_r,t)
  RG_t = max_k | soft(Gamma_t,k + DeltaG_t,k, Kbar lam) - Gamma_t,k | / Kbar
  Gamma_{t+1} = soft(Gamma_t + DeltaG_t, Kbar (lam + omega RG_t))        (step 1 valid: lambda_max(H) <= sum_k |kappa_k|^2 <= 1)

(5) READ, FEEDBACK, LOGITS (unchanged). r_{t+1}(o) = theta_{t+1} phi_t(o) + sum_k Gamma_{t+1,k} kappa_t,k(o). The next block injects W_fb r on the output-canvas tokens. logits = classifier(h) + tau r (or out_ffn).

NESTING. b = 0 (or R_w = 0) together with omega = 0 gives Kbar = 1 and theta_{t+1} = soft(theta_t - (theta_t G_t - S_t + sum Gamma C), lam). That is today's step() exactly.

DALE READING (no code). theta = theta+ - theta-, theta+- >= 0, with theta+-_{t+1} = [theta+-_t +- Delta_t - Kbar(lam + omega R_t)]_+. This has the same fixed points, and theta+ theta- = 0 at the optimum. "LTP-like" means moving the association toward y phi^T; "LTD-like" means moving it toward rhat phi^T, or the uniform depression.

PROPOSITION (fixed points).
Statement: suppose perception has settled (phi_t = phi*, kappa_t = kappa*). Take any window with Kbar > 0 (any |z_r| < 1, any b_r) and any omega in [0,1). Then (theta, Gamma, E, EG) is a fixed point of (1)-(4) iff two things hold: E_r = gamma_r e*/(1 - z_r), and (theta, Gamma) minimises
  J*(theta,Gamma) = (1/2n_l) sum_{l' in others} sum_o w |y - theta phi* - sum_k Gamma_k kappa*_k|^2 + lam (|theta|_1 + |Gamma|_1).
Proof:
- Stationary traces give Delta = Kbar e.
- Suppose R_c > 0. On the support of row c, Kbar e = Kbar(lam + omega R_c) sign(theta), so |soft(u, Kbar lam) - theta| / Kbar = omega R_c there.
- Off the support, |soft(Kbar e, Kbar lam)| / Kbar <= omega R_c.
- Hence R_c <= omega R_c, so R_c = 0 because omega < 1. The same holds for an empty row and for Gamma.
- With R = 0, theta = soft(theta + Kbar e, Kbar lam), which holds iff e is in lam d|theta|_1. These are the lasso KKT conditions, block-wise; for theta and Gamma together they are the KKT conditions of J*. QED
Checked in float64 (24 runs, windows with complex poles, Kbar in {0.41, 2.18, 10}, omega 0.5): max |theta - lasso| <= 3.7e-13, KKT <= 2.6e-15.

replaces_lasso.lasso_function: Selection principle (sparsest consistent theta: minimum l1 among the rules the demonstrations allow)
replaces_lasso.replacement: The fixed point of competition among synapses (the LCA in (1)-(3)). During the transient, selection is the order in which winners are recruited: E%-max admits first the synapses whose unsettled drive is within a fraction (1 - omega) of the strongest one, then relaxes as the population settles. In effect it walks down the l1 regularisation path from lambda_max (continuation), with explaining-away removing early winners that turn out to be redundant.
replaces_lasso.guarantee_or_argument: By the fixed-point proposition, the selected rule is the lasso minimiser for every learned window and every omega < 1. As lam -> 0+ it is therefore the minimum-l1 interpolant: the selection principle is unchanged as a mathematical object and is now explained as competition. The recruitment order matches l1 order when the demonstration code is incoherent: if mutual coherence mu(G*) < 1/(2s-1), the matched-filter winner argmax |S_cj| lies in the true support and the homotopy path adds the support one winner at a time (Tropp 2004; Donoho & Tsaig 2008; both from memory, verify). Under the null-space property alone, early winners can be wrong. The soft circuit can still remove them later; hard WTA cannot. Toy evidence: in the fixed Fourier code a lawful torus rule has exactly one nonzero per row, yet top-1 hard WTA (IHT) solves only 9.1/10.0/9.1% of instances at 150 steps, against 96.3/94.8/95.3% for the soft circuit and the lasso.

replaces_lasso.lasso_function: Explaining-away (decorrelating correlated features through the theta G term)
replaces_lasso.replacement: Lateral inhibition among the synapses onto one colour unit. Its strength G_jk is the co-activity of their presynaptic features over the other demonstrations' labelled cells (anti-Hebbian: own read x pre). There is also cross-inhibition between content synapses and frame synapses through C_k. Only active synapses inhibit.
replaces_lasso.guarantee_or_argument: Algebraic identity: one step at b = 0, omega = 0 is the forward-Euler LCA with dt/tau = 1 (Rozell et al. 2008, eq. 3.2: b = S, inhibition G - I; checked to 2.8e-14). LISTA (Gregor & LeCun 2010) names the same term 'mutual inhibition / explaining away'; Foldiak 1990 is the anti-Hebbian decorrelation precedent. The interaction matrix stays symmetric (G, H): the window acts on the drive e, not on G. So the LCA energy and the convergence argument for the base map (averaged operator, step 1 <= 1/lambda_max because lambda_max(G) <= tr G <= 1) are kept.

replaces_lasso.lasso_function: Noise threshold (lambda ~ kappa/sqrt(n): entries of the Hebbian average below the noise level are set to 0)
replaces_lasso.replacement: A constant depression floor lam, applied uniformly to both Dale populations and scaled by the window's area (Kbar lam). The floor is matched to the gain the window delivers, and it is the only part of the inhibition that survives at stationarity. The E%-max surplus Kbar omega R does not set the noise level: it vanishes at every fixed point.
replaces_lasso.guarantee_or_argument: At a fixed point the threshold is exactly Kbar lam, so the KKT conditions are those of lasso(lam) independently of the window (proposition). The principled value is still the standard error of the Hebbian average, kappa/sqrt(n_l) (universal threshold, Donoho & Johnstone 1994, from memory; repo prior kappa = 0.145). The learned scalar lam_raw is kept as is, because E1 shows lam's value is not load-bearing at <=10. 'Competition = net LTD' is the literature anchor: Song, Miller & Abbott 2000 need net depression for synaptic competition. Here the net depression is the floor plus the surplus.

replaces_lasso.lasso_function: Guarantee (theorem 0: S, L, I via the null-space property, and C imply the exact query answer)
replaces_lasso.replacement: Theorem 0 restated for the circuit: location is exact, attraction is a premise, recovery is unchanged. The temporal kernel and the WTA surplus are 'rate terms' that vanish at stationarity, so they cannot move the guarantee.
replaces_lasso.guarantee_or_argument:
(a) Location (proved, unconditional in the window and in omega < 1): fixed points = minimisers of J* on the settled code phi*.
(b) Recovery (verbatim theorem 0): S, L and I (NSP in phi*-coordinates) with lam -> 0+ imply the minimiser is the true rule and the query argmax is exact. At finite lam, under the irrepresentable condition with sign consistency, theta_S = theta*_S - lam G_SS^-1 sign(theta*_S), and the argmax is exact when the query margin exceeds lam |phi_S(o*)^T G_SS^-1 sign| (checked to 1.25e-12 earlier; Fuchs / Zhao & Yu / Wainwright, from memory). Colour-uniform K and omega keep the argmax (no per-colour gains), and no per-feature gains means no weighted-lasso distortion.
(c) Attraction (premise C):
- Proved for b = 0, omega = 0 (ISTA, step 1 < 2/lambda_max).
- On a fixed active set with the default real lobe it is heavy ball (stable for beta < 1 since lambda_max <= 1).
- With the surplus it is observed, not proved: float64 runs converged for every tested window at omega 0.5. A same-time step above 1 combined with omega >= 0.6 stalled (KKT 0.056 after 1e5 steps), which is why K(0) = 1 is fixed and omega is capped.
- Provable variant: multiply the surplus and the lobe by a summable envelope (inexact Krasnosel'skii-Mann iteration).
(d) Why soft and not hard: with noiseless demonstrations every exact fit whose entries exceed the threshold is a hard-threshold fixed point, so selection moves into the path, and an IHT guarantee needs RIP of order 3s rather than NSP (Blumensath & Davies). Earlier check: IHT recovered 0.50 vs lasso 1.00 at n=30. Condition N and proposition 4 are unchanged: no new cross-lane operation, and the traces contain only the lane's own drive, which is built from other lanes' labels.

design:guarantee-first.story:
Working title of the section: "What survives stationarity."

(1) Lineage, with no new terms:
- The Hebbian outer product becomes fast weights and linear attention (Schlag et al. 2021), and then the delta rule (DeltaNet).
- The rule synapse is the same delta rule solved over the demonstration set (leave-one-out within the task's group), plus competition among synapses.
- Its drive e = (y - rhat) phi^T is the hetero-associative form of TEM's memory update M <- lam M + eta (p - phat)(p + phat)^T (Whittington et al. 2020, STAR Methods): Hebbian with the observation, anti-Hebbian with the prediction.

(2) One window, two jobs:
- A pair-based window over recursion depth splits into its area (the Hebbian term) and a zero-area remainder (filtered rates of pre and post): Xie & Seung's beta0 Hebb + beta1 pre x dpost/dt.
- The bands memory and the rule synapse use the same window parametrisation (poles z_r = exp(-e^nu + i vartheta), weights b_r) but sit on opposite sides of this split.
- In perception both pre and post move along recursion, the area is free, and the learned Sudoku kernels bring the net fixed-point Hebbian gain near 0 in 7 of 8 heads. Our reading, offered as an interpretation: they record change.
- In the rule synapse the pre is a feature code that settles and the teacher is constant. Only the area survives at a fixed point. The area is the delta rule's step, and scaling the depression floor by it makes every window give the same fixed point.
- What the shape still does is the path: the post-leading lobe pairs past errors with present features, which on the active set is heavy-ball momentum.

(3) Competition:
- The synapses onto a colour unit inhibit one another in proportion to the co-activity of their presynaptic features over the other demonstrations (explaining away, an LCA).
- All synapses are depressed uniformly (constant LTD, Dale split).
- E%-max feedback inhibition admits only synapses within a fraction of the strongest unsettled drive, and relaxes as the synapses settle.
- TEM's structure/content factorisation appears as two kinds of competing hypotheses in one population: frames (Gamma, structure: where to read) and content synapses (theta, what colour). The frame reads are themselves softmax retrievals, i.e. soft WTA over input cells (Hopfield/attention).
- Short version: WTA where the operation is retrieval, convex competition where it is inference.

(4) The guarantee:
- Fixed points equal the lasso for every learned window and competition strength, so theorem 0 holds verbatim.
- Hard WTA is the counterexample that motivates soft competition: every exact fit is a fixed point, so selection moves into the start state, and the guarantee would need RIP instead of NSP.

(5) What the path buys (existence check, fixed Fourier code, no learning, all 3,072 torus instances):
- 16 steps: the circuit answers 79.6%, the best-thresholded FISTA lasso 57.7%.
- At convergence every soft variant gives 96.3/94.8/95.3%.

(6) The same principle in search:
- The torus search's dopamine term failed to consolidate because its baseline did not vanish at the solution, so it moved the fixed point.
- A modulator that vanishes there should fix it (experiment E3).

Paper sentence: in the rule synapse, stationarity separates the guarantee (Hebbian area + competition = lasso) from the search (window shape, WTA surplus). ARC-2 stays outside, as a hypothesis-family (S) limitation.
